articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Sale Sharks defy Jacques Vermeulen's first-half red card to beat Saracens
articles.summary: Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen's first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O'Flaherty emerging as the star of a slugfest at StoneX Stadium.
articles.body:
Sale Sharks' Jacques Vermeulen received a 20-minute red card for a tackle on Tomos Williams in the first half; Sale's Alex Lozowski had also seen yellow for a similar offence; Sale managed to hold on and get the win

Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen's first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O'Flaherty emerging as the star of a slugfest at StoneX Stadium.

Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.

Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O'Flaherty produced the match's pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try.

It was part of a dominant second half from Sale, who capitalised on the hosts' lifeless performance to bounce back after losing to Bristol on the opening weekend with their hooker Nathan Jibulu also outstanding.

Referee Joe James and TMO Hamish Smales experienced a busy opening half an hour, issuing two cards and disallowing a Saracens try.

It had started so well for Sale when Jibulu finished a driving maul but soon after centre Lozowski was sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on Alfie Barbeary, who was forced off for an HIA.

Worse was to come when Vermeulen was given his marching orders for a dangerous challenge on Williams as the Sharks looked to press home an attack down the right touchline.

It meant Saracens were given the opportunity to play against 13 for three minutes and Sale's situation would have deteriorated further had Courtney Lawes not seen an attempted deliberate knock go backwards.

Almost immediately the hosts appeared to have taken advantage but a Nick Tompkins try was ruled out because of obstruction by Nick Isiekwe and it was not until Eroni Mawi bundled over in the 34th minute that they were off the mark.

For all Saracens' sustained pressure they still trailed 7-5 and a minute into the second half that became 14-5 after O'Flaherty caught a George Ford up and under that went sideways and then slipped through the home defence before sprinting over.

Sale ran out of tacklers to enable Sione Va'enuku to strike back almost immediately but they resumed on the front foot and were frustrated to be penalised just short of the whitewash on two occasions.

They continued knocking on the door and suddenly changed pace with a series of runs gaining yards until Ford sent Ben Bamber galloping over.

Sale now led 21-10 and Saracens' dismal afternoon continued when Theo Dan limped off while his fellow hooker Jamie George watched from the stands, sidelined by injury.

Charlie Bracken combined with brother Jack to race over with eight minutes to go and the Sharks then let another commanding position slip away because of a penalty close to the line, but they had already done enough to see off Saracens.

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Bath beat Exeter Chiefs in pulsating West Country derby to move top of table
articles.summary: Bath beat Exeter Chiefs 40-34 in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec to take them to the top of the Gallagher Prem table but they were made to fight all the way in an 11-try thriller.
articles.body:
Bath climb to top of table after claiming derby honours in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec; they avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat to Exeter in another thriller

Bath beat Exeter Chiefs 40-34 in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec to take them to the top of the Gallagher Prem table but they were made to fight all the way in an 11-try thriller.

Exeter trailed 26-10 at the interval but rallied to lead 33-31 midway through the second half before a yellow card for scrum-half Stephen Varney eventually proved decisive.

Cam Redpath, Dan du Preez, Bernard van der Linde, Ted Hill and Finn Russell scored Bath's tries. There was also a penalty try award with Russell converting four.

The hugely impressive Immanuel Feyi-Waboso scored two tries for Exeter with Jack Yeandle, Josh Iosefa-Scott and Varney also going over. Henry Slade converted three and Harvey Skinner added a late penalty.

Bath took control as first Redpath intercepted a Skinner pass to run 50 metres and score before Van der Linde slipped through a gap in the visitors' defence for an individual try. Russell converted both to give his side a 14-0 lead at the end of the first quarter.

Exeter badly needed a response and they got one thanks to the strong running of Feyi-Waboso. First he evaded a tackle from Ollie Lawrence to put the defence on the back foot and when the ball was recycled he powered past another two coverers with Varney on hand to touchdown.

The hosts scored their third try when a favourable bounce on halfway saw them capitalise with Van der Linde and Ewan Richards taking advantage to give Du Preez the chance to force his way over from close range but Bath bungled the kick-off so Yeandle was able to keep his side in contention with a try from a driving lineout.

However with half-time approaching, Bath exerted a period of pressure culminating in Russell dummying his way over for the bonus-point try before converting for a 26-10 interval lead.

Exeter began the second half strongly and were rewarded with two tries in quick succession. First Iosefa-Scott crashed over from close range before Feyi-Waboso took his opportunity in style by brushing aside two would-be tacklers. Slade converted both and his side were right back in the contest with just two points between the teams.

Exeter took the lead for the first time when former Bath man Will Butt carved the hosts apart to provide Feyi-Waboso with an easy run-in for his second try.

The home side were soon awarded a penalty try with Varney yellow-carded for a deliberate knock-on and in the scrum-half's absence, Hill battered his way over the tryline.

Slade missed badly with a penalty attempt so Skinner took over the goal-kicking and his success gave Chiefs two deserved bonus points from the match.

articles.title: Zoe Stratford gives birth to baby girl - a year after England World Cup triumph
articles.summary: Zoe Stratford, who captained England to World Cup glory a year ago, gives birth to a baby girl.
articles.body:
England's World Cup-winning captain Zoe Stratford has given birth to her first child.

Stratford - nee Aldcroft - gave birth to a baby girl, who is currently nameless, on Wednesday.

England beat Canada in the World Cup final in September 2025.

Stratford, 29, joined Sale Sharks from Gloucester-Hartpury in the summer, having played a key role in their rise to become the dominant force in the women's domestic game.

Commenting on an Instagram , external post announcing the birth by Stratford's husband Luke, Sale said: "The most amazing news!"

Stratford was named World Player of the Year in 2021 and co-captained Gloucester-Hartpury to three back-to-back Premiership Women's Rugby titles.

She was the third England women's player to announce she was expecting this year, following Bristol's Lark Atkin-Davies and Abbie Ward.

In April England team-mates Marlie Packer and Rosie Galligan announced they are expecting a baby together, with lock Galligan due to give birth this month.

Meg Jones, who was named England captain after Stratford's pregnancy announcement, has recently called for England players to have access to fertility support and egg freezing.

articles.title: Ireland v Japan: Jane Clohessy and Niamh Gallagher to make first starts
articles.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand hands first starts to Jane Clohessy and Niamh Gallagher for Saturday's Test with Japan.
articles.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has handed first starts to Jane Clohessy and Niamh Gallagher for Saturday's Test with Japan.

The trio of Sophie Barrett, Kate Jordan and Alana McInerney are set to make their Ireland debuts off the bench.

Ireland defeated Japan in the WXV Global Series in Galway on Sunday and the sides will face off again in a Test at Virgin Media Park in Cork.

Bemand's side are back in WXV action with a double-header with South Africa later in October.

Munster's Clohessy will win her third cap with a maiden start in the second row, while full-back Gallagher has been named in the starting team for the first time.

Despite the chance to offer new faces experience, there are also plenty of experienced names in Bemand's line-up.

Linda Djougang, Neve Jones and Eilis Cahill make up the front row, with Clohessy and Fiona Tuite-O'Sullivan in the second row.

Erin King captains the side from flanker, and she is joined in the back row by Brittany Hogan and Jemima Adams Verling.

Emily Lane and Dannah O'Brien retain their half-back partnership, while Anna McGann, who has won the majority of her 19 Ireland caps on the wing, will partner Aoife Dalton at centre.

The back three is made up of Beibhinn Parsons and Robyn O'Connor, who join Gallagher on her first start.

Key back row Aoife Wafer will not be risked in the Test after a "minor" training injury kept her out of the team to face Japan last Sunday.

Replacements: Beth Buttimer, Sadhbh McGrath, Sophie Barrett, Kate Jordan, Grace Moore, Aoibheann Reilly, Enya Breen, Alana McInerney.

articles.title: Dragons 38-26 Scarlets: Six-try hosts seal URC Welsh derby success
articles.summary: Dragons secure a Welsh derby win in a United Rugby Championship (URC) 10-try thrilling encounter at Rodney Parade in Newport.
articles.body:
Tries: Tuitavuki, Dee 2 , Martinez, Anderson, Hunt Cons: de Beer 3 , J Lloyd

Tries : Page 2 , S O'Connor, I Jones Cons: Costelow 3

Dragons secured a Welsh derby win in the United Rugby Championship (URC), beating Scarlets in a 10-try thriller at Rodney Parade.

Two tries from Wales hooker Elliot Dee, and further scores from wing Anzelo Tuitavuki, props Rodrigo Martinez and Rob Hunt and full-back Huw Anderson sealed the six-try success.

Scarlets responded with two tries from wing Macs Page and scores from replacements Sam O'Connor and Ioan Jones.

The match was played in front of a raucous crowd of 7,163, which created a memorable occasion in Newport.

Dragons are unbeaten, following up the opening weekend draw with Benetton, while Scarlets, who are missing influential injured back-row duo Taine Plumtree and Fletcher Anderson, have suffered two derby defeats, having also lost at home to Cardiff.

Scarlets prop Domachowski ruled out for two months

Dragons trio continuing Gwent's Tongan tradition

Groves' journey from heart surgery to Scarlets

Wales fly-half Sam Costelow was among five personnel changes from the Scarlets team that lost 21-15 to Cardiff, with Wales props Kemsley Mathias and Harri O'Connor, lock Alex Groves and flanker Dan Davis starting.

Dragons co-captain Ben Carter returned to lead the side that drew 19-19 with Benetton , but fellow skipper Angus O'Brien was still missing.

Dee, Hunt, and back-row duo Shane Lewis-Hughes and Harri Keddie were also included.

Scrum-half Rhodri Williams led the side out with his family on his 150th Dragons appearance against his former team, where he spent five seasons.

The two teams ran out to easily the most fervent atmosphere of a Welsh home match so far this season, with the fixture benefiting from its sunny Saturday afternoon kick-off time.

It was the away fans who were celebrating first as Page scored a superb solo try after drifting around the Dragons defence before collecting his own chip.

The hosts responded with a period of pressure and were rewarded with a first Dragons try for Tongan wing Tuitavuki.

This inspired the hosts as they kept up the pressure with a well-worked line-out between centre Aneurin Owen and flanker Thomas Young, which laid the platform for another attacking set-piece that yielded a driving try for Dee.

Scarlets scrum-half Dane Blacker sought to install some tempo in the visitors' play, and an attacking scrum allowed centre Eddie James to burst through the middle, before a long Costelow floated pass released Page to stroll in for his second.

Costelow converted as Scarlets led 14-12 at half-time.

Dragons dominate second half to seal win

Dragons struck straight after the break when wing Rio Dyer took the ball superbly from kick-off to put the hosts on the front foot.

After subtle build-up work from de Beer and Anderson, a searing Tuitavuki break was only halted by a brilliant tap tackle from Scarlets full-back Blair Murray, but Argentina prop Martinez followed up to cross, with de Beer converting.

Scarlets retaliated and, following another midfield charge from James, a perfect Page chip narrowly eluded Mee's hands as he lost possession over the Dragons line.

The home side brought on Wales props Rhodri Jones and Dillon Lewis and the duo forced a scrum penalty.

Scarlets replacement prop Sam O'Connor made his own early impression when he burrowed over for the third try.

Costelow's conversion regained the lead, but Scarlets put themselves under pressure with needless penalties from the kick-off.

Dragons flanker Young was held up over the line, but it was Anderson who scored the bonus-point try in the right-hand corner to give the Dragons the advantage once more.

Dyer produced an excellent break, and Scarlets captain Josh Macleod could only stop the momentum with a professional foul that resulted in a yellow card.

The hosts took control with Dee driven over for his second score, which proved his final act before being replaced.

Scarlets, playing with 14 men, struck back quickly with a quick line-out before replacement Jones crossed for the bonus-point try.

Dragons gathered themselves and Hunt's final try sealed the success in what was a fourth try on the day for the home front-row.

Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia: "We had all the possession and territory in the first half but just weren't clinical enough.

"We were in control and needed to maximise the opportunities when they were on.

"I am proud of the group. We want to keep growing and keep going up the ladder."

articles.title: Lions 35-19 Ospreys: South Africans fight back for URC win at Ellis Park
articles.summary: Ospreys beaten in Johannesburg after six-try Lions turn around half-time deficit in the United Rugby Championship.
articles.body:
Tries: Cronje, Botha, Brandon, Chamberlain, Mpeku 2 Con: Smith Pens: Smith

Tries: K Williams, Daniel, Moriarty Cons: Edwards 2

Ospreys were comprehensively beaten by six-try Lions after a second-half onslaught at Ellis Park in the United Rugby Championship.

Mark Jones' Ospreys started the 2026-27 season by claiming a four-try bonus point in defeat by Sharks in Durban, but they left Johannesburg without anything to show for their efforts on Saturday.

Ospreys led 12-10 at half-time after responding excellently to Erich Cronje's opener with tries by Keiran Williams and Efan Daniel.

But Lions, who enjoyed set-piece dominance, had their four-try bonus secured before the hour thanks to PJ Botha, Morne Brandon and Boeta Chamberlain.

Kelly Mpeku added two more for Lions, while Ospreys scored their third through Ross Moriarty with the final play.

An off-day from the kicking tee for the prolific Lions fly-half Chris Smith, who could only manage one conversion and a penalty, prevented this from being an absolute hammering.

Ospreys have the consolation of knowing their South Africa tour is out of the way early on.

They now return to Wales for a derby against Dragons at Rodney Parade on Friday, 9 October (19:45 BST).

Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

Ospreys won against Lions at altitude in Johannesburg in the 2023-24 Challenge Cup, but repeating that in the URC was always going to be a long shot.

The hosts lost just once on home soil last season – to South African rivals Bulls – and started the current campaign with victory against Leinster.

The only score of a scrappy first quarter was a penalty by Smith, with Ospreys turning down opportunities to level in favour of hunting a try.

It was Lions who were first to cross in the 28th minute through wing Cronje after an incisive attack from turnover ball.

Ospreys responded well and struck back, also from turnover ball, when centre Williams cut a nice line to finish powerfully from midfield partner Evardi Boshoff's offload.

It got better when they exploited Lions' indiscipline to get a second try with the last play of the half through hooker Daniel from a driving line-out.

Opposite number Botha and replacement Brandon scored through the same method soon after the restart to get the home side back on track.

Lions got their bonus point in the 57th minute when full-back Chamberlain crossed, with Francke Horn's athletic offload deemed to have been flat.

Wales fly-half Dan Edwards was yellow-carded for a high tackle on the hour, and the hosts turned the screw with wing Mpeku going over twice down the right.

Replacement flanker Moriarty did prevent Ospreys from suffering a scoreless second half, but this was another statement of intent by Lions at home in their bid to qualify for successive play-offs.

articles.title: Rugby World Cup 2027: Wales preparations outlined a year out from Australia
articles.summary: With one year to go before the 2027 Rugby World Cup, what lies in wait for Steve Tandy's Wales over the next 12 months before they head to Australia?
articles.body:
It might be hard to believe how quickly it comes around, but Thursday marks a year to go until the men's Rugby World Cup begins in Australia.

The 2027 competition starts on 1 October in Perth with a match between Australia and Hong Kong China, with the tournament finale on 13 November in Sydney.

Wales are to feature in the second game when they open their campaign against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October.

Steve Tandy's side sit 11th in the world rankings, currently topped by reigning World Cup champions South Africa.

The tournament has expanded from 20 to 24 teams, with the number of pools rising from four to six.

All 12 teams who finished inside the top three of their pools at the 2023 World Cup - France, New Zealand, Italy, Ireland, South Africa, Scotland, Wales, Fiji, Australia, England, Argentina and Japan - qualified automatically.

Georgia, Spain, Romania, Portugal, Tonga, Canada, United States of America, Uruguay, Chile, Zimbabwe, Hong Kong China and Samoa all earned their places through qualifying tournaments.

Wales have 12 or 13 potential matches across three blocks before they travel to Australia.

Nations Championship home matches are set to be staged against Japan, New Zealand and Australia in November, before a final play-off game at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

There will be five matches in the 2027 Six Nations, with trips to play France, Scotland and Italy and home fixtures in Cardiff against England and Ireland.

Following the end of the 2026-27 domestic season, Wales will meet up in the summer for fitness camps, with past trips including visits to Poland, Switzerland and Turkey.

There will be three or four World Cup warm-ups in the summer. The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has so far refused to publicly announce who they will face next August and September, or even how many games they will play.

The likely scenario is that Wales will play three games in Europe before a warm-up match on the way to or in Australia itself.

Tandy held alignment camps with more than 50 players in September, and the World Cup squad will eventually be whittled down to the final 33.

Wales have been drawn in Pool F alongside England, Tonga and Zimbabwe and will travel to play at three different venues.

The opening game against Zimbabwe will be staged in Adelaide, followed by a six-day turnaround before they face Tonga in Melbourne.

England await eight days later in Sydney on 16 October, before the expanded knockout stages.

Next year's World Cup will feature 16 teams at the knockout phase, rather than the traditional eight who previously went straight to the quarter-finals.

The top two teams from each of the six pools will progress to the last 16 alongside the four best third-place nations.

If Wales were to win their group, they would play the runner-up from pool B, which contains South Africa, Italy, Georgia and Romania.

Should Wales finish second, they would face the second-placed side in pool C, which is made up of Argentina, Fiji, Spain and Canada.

South Africa and New Zealand, World Cup finalists in 2023, are destined to meet in the quarter-finals, set to be staged in Sydney and Brisbane, if they top their groups.

The Olympic Stadium in Sydney will host both semi-finals and the bronze medal match, before staging the showpiece final on Saturday, 13 November.

articles.title: Never played in The Prem, now they face hosts Australia in 2027 World Cup opener
articles.summary: Jack Combes and Alex Post tell BBC Sport about a "dream come true" as they look ahead to the 2027 Rugby World Cup opener against hosts Australia.
articles.body:
It is 1 October 2027. There are 61,000 fans inside Perth Stadium.

There is a global TV audience in the millions as two teams go through their final warm-ups preparing to open the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

For hosts Australia, twice world champions with a proud rugby history across the codes, it is familiar territory.

For their opponents Hong Kong China, it is anything but.

It will be their World Cup debut and for their players it will be biggest match of their lives.

Among them, all being well, are Jack Combes and Alex Post. Two players more used to the lower semi-professional tiers of the English league system than the global spotlight.

It is David v Goliath - in football parlance it is Spain v Cape Verde.

Twelve months earlier to the day, Jack and Alex are in Hong Kong. It is a national holiday and both have taken time out to tell BBC Sport about how their sporting and personal lives have been transformed.

"I think the whole run-up to the whole qualification process was already a dream in itself. To qualify for a men's first World Cup was huge," said Combes, a scrum-half.

There are glints in their eyes and smiles on their faces - why wouldn't there be?

Hong Kong China have been drawn in Pool A at the World Cup, where not just the hosts await, but also Chile - and the All Blacks.

"People will say it's daunting and it's a huge challenge to have those two top nations in your pool, but if you're going to do it, do it properly. Why not?" said Combes.

"People might question whether we deserve to be there. But for me, if you asked anyone as a kid, if you could open up the World Cup in that first game in a year's time, it's genuinely amazing. A dream come true.

"And I'm sure anyone who does give us any criticism about us being there, there's no way they wouldn't be doing the same thing if they could, 100%."

Despite having made his international debut a decade ago, until recently Post was hooking for Richmond in The Champ.

"Unfortunately, I've never played at The Prem level. But The Champ definitely doesn't get the credit it deserves," said the 31-year-old.

"It's a very tough league. And that was great preparation for the international games."

Post was a full-time rugby player with Hong Kong China, before the Covid pandemic brought that to an end and he began a Masters degree at the University of Oxford.

The Varsity match at Twickenham remains one of the larger crowds he has played in front of.

"One of the unique selling points for Hong Kong is the players are contracted all year round and spend all their time together," said Post.

"So it wasn't really feasible for players like myself to stay at Richmond.

"Hong Kong was very much, 'we need boots on the ground'.

"I've moved my family and myself over the last couple of weeks and yeah, kind of chase the dream for the next year."

A full-time professional contract has enabled greater focus on the game away from being a financial analyst.

"With Richmond, we'd train twice a week and then you would do your own gym sessions in your own time," added Post.

"But you can probably do twice as much as that with Hong Kong now."

For Combes, 29, a former student and teacher at Hartpury College, it has been a circuitous route to professional sport that included a spell at Birmingham Moseley in England's third tier.

"So I've been full-time in the sevens for about three and a half years now," he said.

"I've done my career in reverse. I went from teaching after an ACL (anterior cruciate ligament injury), to playing semi-professional rugby, to being a full-time athlete at the age of 25.

"I wouldn't change it for the world, but going into a full-time environment where you have the resources, you have the training time, physical development, it's necessary for what we're facing."

Hong Kong has a proud tradition of rugby stretching back seven decades, not least around its annual sevens tournament.

They qualified for the World Cup by defeating Korea 70-22 in the final round of the Asia Rugby Championship last year.

A late 42-40 victory over fellow World Cup finalists Uruguay in July was perhaps the strongest showing yet of where they stand.

"The mindset's changed from years gone by where you compete in Asia and you play against teams that you know you probably should be beating," said Combes.

"Now we're completely on the other side of the spectrum where we've got nothing to lose.

"I think just be ambitious, be fearless, and go for it.

"'Be memorable' is the phrase that coaches have been talking about."

Both Post and Combes were born in Hong Kong and came up through the age-grade system there. They have witnessed how the game has grown there and are aware of the criticism they have faced, often focused on the international make-up of the team.

"It's always the first criticism we get after an international game," said Post.

"We don't go looking for that criticism or feedback. But it's always going to be there. I think for us, just perform and try and put something out there that people are proud of."

"I was born here in 1997," added Combes.

"Mum is half Chinese and going through the whole minis rugby here where we probably had one of the biggest mini rugby numbers base in the world, up until Covid.

"But I think the game's back growing within local schools - primary, secondary.

"Hopefully we can inspire the next generation."

Former London Irish and Ospreys director of rugby Toby Booth has joined the coaching set-up.

A good test of where they are at will come when Hong Kong China take on three countries in the Nations Cup next month, all with World Cup heritage, in the shape of USA, Canada and Tonga.

"Personally, I've got a whole bunch of pressure just from my family and friends," said Post.

"I've been getting messages all today saying it's one year, you better make the team.

"There will definitely be a big Hong Kong contingent [in Perth]. We want to be everyone's second team."

"You know, we are always going to be the underdogs," said Combes, who is known to his team-mates as Maradona for his keenness to kick any stray footballs that make their way on to the training pitch.

"I think our whole string of games leading into the World Cup with Nations Cup, warm-up games we're always going to be sort of looked over.

"But I think that works in our favour - we're just a bit fearless."

Oh, and remember Spain v Cape Verde at the Fifa World Cup? That ended in a draw.

articles.title: Josh Adams: Wales and Cardiff wing targets third Rugby World Cup
articles.summary: Wales wing Josh Adams is nearing full fitness in time for the autumn internationals and looking forward to a World Cup trip to Australia next year.
articles.body:
Wales wing Josh Adams says he would love to play in a third World Cup as he targets a first trip to Australia next year.

It is exactly a year until Wales play their opening game against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October, before further pool games against Tonga and England.

"I'm desperate to go, but there is loads of rugby to be played and months ahead of us," said Adams, looking ahead to the tournament.

"It is important that you navigate your way through correctly and get to that start line in a good spot to be selected."

Adams, 31, was the World Cup's top try scorer in the 2019 tournament in Japan with seven as Wales reached the semi-finals.

The Cardiff back, who was also part of the squad that lost a quarter-final to Argentina four years later, insists he is just as excited for a hat-trick of global tournaments.

"I've never been to Australia, so that, as well as playing in a World Cup, is something I'm determined to do," said Adams.

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

The Warm Up: One Year To The Rugby World Cup!

Wales begin the World Cup countdown by playing four matches in the second half of the Nations Championship in November.

Japan, New Zealand and Australia will travel to play in Cardiff before a final play-off match at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham.

Adams was ruled out of Wales' 43-0 defeat by South Africa in Durban in July due to a calf injury.

The British and Irish Lions wing has missed Cardiff's start to the season but says he will be fit for international duty next month, with a club return expected in October.

"I am training, but it's important that you navigate your way through correctly and there's no rush," said Adams.

"I had the calf injury in the summer, but I've been good for a while.

"It's making sure that when I'm playing, I'm 100% fit and healthy, and I've had good preparation time."

articles.title: Alex Groves' journey from heart surgery to Scarlets
articles.summary: New Scarlets lock Alex Groves describes his remarkable return to rugby following heart surgery.
articles.body:
New Scarlets lock Alex Groves will make his home debut on Saturday when he lines up against the Dragons in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

The fact the 25-year-old is playing at all is remarkable considering he underwent major eight-hour heart surgery in February 2024.

There was not just a question whether he would play again. There was even concern about his survival.

"I was confident as a young boy that I was fit and healthy and never thought anything was wrong with me. It was such a shock when I found out.

"It went very quickly from 'do I need surgery?' to 'am I still going to be playing rugby?' - to 'am I still going be alive in two years' time?'."

Carter and Costelow back for Welsh derby

Scarlets prop Domachowski ruled out for two months

Groves was born and brought up in Johannesburg but, aged 19, moved to join Bristol and would help England Under-20s win a Grand Slam.

As part of Bristol's pre-season preparations in 2021, Groves and his team-mates underwent cardio screenings unavailable to the public without symptoms. After the tests he was informed he had a leaky valve in his heart.

The 6ft 9in (2.06m) lock was told it was nothing abnormal, that one in four people have the issue, and that it would just need to be monitored.

In April 2022 Groves joined Sale Sharks, and during another similar heart screening he was told his situation had deteriorated.

The view of medical experts was that he would need surgery within the next five years to stop his heart from growing to a size where it would not be able to support itself.

On 5 January 2024, Groves' 23rd birthday, he was then told about the discovery of an aneurysm - an abnormal bulge in the wall of a blood vessel - that needed urgent attention.

"I remember they found the problem in August 2023 and from there it was on and off for a couple of months," said Groves.

"I had a test in December and then on my birthday the following year, I went in and saw my surgeon with my parents in Liverpool.

"Thank God my parents were in that meeting with me because I completely shut off and everything my surgeon told me from that point on I did not take in.

“It literally scared the life out of me and I didn't actually retain any information.

"I was on the car ride home back to Manchester and my parents were having to relay all the information.”

He recalled how an initial diagnosis had also been missed because of his unusual height.

"My surgeon said I could not play because they'd found an aneurysm that they'd missed," said Groves.

"That was purely down to the fact MRI machines aren't really built for six foot nine broad-shouldered people.

"I remember getting into that machine and sort of squishing up and by doing that, the extra body mass over my heart meant they missed it.

"But fortunately they found it because one wrong hit to the chest and I would've bled out in a matter of seconds because it was on my aortic artery."

Groves had been planning to play in a Champions Cup match for Sale against Stormers in South Africa in January but had to withdraw.

A month later he was having major surgery. He was on the operating table for eight hours.

"It was terrifying but I think it is more scary for the people closest to you," said Groves.

"I just fell asleep and woke up. But I had my girlfriend at the time and my mum sitting in the waiting room.

Groves said he had been put at ease by the medics before the operation.

"I remember speaking to my anaesthetist who was a big rugby fan," recalled Groves.

"He told me the procedure they were doing was as easy as it is for me as a lock to jump in the line-out.

"It's amazing they're able to do something like that at that level of ease. I thought then I'm going to be fine.

"It's amazing how advanced things have become now.

“If I was a player in my position 10 years ago they probably wouldn't have found the problem.

"Or I would have had to retire or even sadly have passed away.”

Groves spent the next nine months recovering and praised Sale for their part in helping him return to fitness.

The South African-born forward has previously spoken about his lack of motivation during that period, , external and how with different heart rhythms he was sweating and out of breath just climbing up stairs.

"It was a tough rehabilitation process," said Groves.

"Sale Sharks weren't obviously familiar with the process of a patient that has to go through open heart surgery.

Groves was given the all-clear to play again in November 2024 and was loaned out to Championship side Caldy RFC.

He returned to the field in late December in a Championship match against Ealing Trailfinders, 10 months after his surgery.

“Thankfully it was a success,” said Groves.

“I've never had a problem since. It's good as new to be honest.”

Groves left Sale in 2025 and returned to South Africa where he joined the Stormers.

He had a brief period loaned to Scarlets when they went to South Africa, Groves helping the Welsh region solve a lock-injury crisis, starting against Lions and coming off the bench against Sharks.

He joined the Llanelli club permanently for the 2026-27 season and has been embraced by some Scarlets fans his family met in Johannesburg during the Lions game - those supporters are sponsoring Groves during his stay in Wales.

They also helped him with some early accommodation when Groves spent six weeks in a flat above a pub in Llanelli, with the owners helping him settle in.

Groves, who has since moved, made his competitive debut as a replacement in the 21-15 defeat against Cardiff last weekend.

And he is enjoying his time back on the field in a new environment.

"It put things into perspective," said Groves.

"It made me realise how fortunate I am to do what I love and have the family and support I have around me.

"It sort of matured me in a way at a young age. I'm just grateful to be here still doing what I love."

articles.title: Christian Wade: Newcastle winger close to record in try-dominated Prem
articles.summary: Christian Wade sits four away from Chris Ashton's all-time record of 101 as tries dominate Prem Rugby.
articles.body:
The opening week of the new Prem season was all about tries, tries, tries as the league's 10 teams went on all-out attack.

No fewer than 52 tries were scored across the five matches, setting a record for the opening round of a season, with an average of more than 10 per game and four players claiming hat-tricks as spectators were royally entertained.

Contributing two of those scores was Christian Wade for Newcastle Red Bulls in their 59-26 loss at Northampton Saints, as the veteran winger moves closer to an all-time record.

The 35-year-old is now on 97 career tries in the Prem, only four behind Chris Ashton's record mark of 101.

If Wade stays fit and the Red Bulls continue to play a game where they want to get the ball wide, it's surely only a matter of time before the record is in his hands.

Listen to commentary from BBC Radio Newcastle and BBC Radio Leicester

Wade returned to rugby union last December with Newcastle after a short spell in rugby league with Wigan Warriors and he made no secret of his desire to chase down Ashton's tally .

He only added two last season as the Red Bulls struggled at the bottom, but his two tries on the opening night away to the champions suggest new-look Newcastle are going to be nothing if not entertaining.

It is more than 15 years since Wade scored his first try in Prem Rugby for Wasps but anyone watching his efforts at Franklin's Gardens would not have seen a player of diminishing powers - rather, they would have admired the enduring speed and slipperiness of the Newcastle winger.

"Christian bounces across in front of people where they can't lay a finger on him," Red Bulls head coach Dan McFarland told BBC Sport.

"He can accelerate through a hole and defenders find it very difficult to cope with that."

101 - Chris Ashton (Northampton, Saracens, Sale, Harlequins, Worcester, Leicester)

97 - Christian Wade (Wasps, Gloucester, Newcastle)

92 - Tom Varndell (Leicester, Wasps, Bristol)

72 - Mike Brown (Harlequins, Newcastle, Leicester)

69 - Paul Sackey (Bedford, London Irish, Wasps, Harlequins)

Wade's Prem tries have come for Wasps, Gloucester and now Newcastle across a globetrotting 15-year career.

His sporting journey has also taken in a spell in France with Racing 92 in the Top 14, the 13-man code with Wigan and more than three years in the NFL with the Buffalo Bills, even though he never made it into their main squad.

And that period in America has left an indelible mark, according to his new head coach, as to why Wade remains a feared Prem opponent.

"Christian Wade is a proper professional," said McFarland. "He spent a few years in the NFL and he's clearly taken a lot from that experience in terms of how to look after himself and how to prepare himself as a rugby player.

"He's a really good team man, he's got a lot of time for the young players. He's always calm, a calming and connecting influence.

"Christian's in our leadership group because of his capacity to be able to connect with people. He's a really good person."

Leading Prem try scorers in last five seasons

2025-26: 18 - Tommy Freeman (Northampton), Noah Caluori

2024-25: 13 - Gabriel Ibitoye (Bristol), Ollie Hassell-Collins (Leicester)

2023-24: 14 - Ollie Sleightholme (Northampton)

With Wade four short of equalling Ashton's 101 tally and five tries away from breaking it, the current record holder can feel him coming.

The Slough-born winger is the only player in the top 10 still actively playing, but Ashton believes the mark is eventually going to go a long way past 101 with the type of rugby on offer in the modern Prem.

Last year's top try scorers, Northampton and England's Tommy Freeman and Saracens' teenage starlet Noah Caluori both touched down 18 times, the highest season-ending figure for five years, while Caluori's tally included him scoring five tries per match on two separate occasions against Sale Sharks.

Freeman started this campaign with a hat-trick in the same game as Wade's double and that took his career mark to 58, all at the age of 25.

With the England winger having signed a new contract at Saints and their dynamic games delivering tries by the barrel load, could he be the player to eventually take the record?

"It's happening [the record being broken], but it's not going to last long, whoever takes it," Ashton told BBC's Rugby Union Weekly podcast.

"I think it's going to be absolutely blown to smithereens.

"I sat there on Friday and watched Tommy run in another hat-trick and thought he's going to get 20 this year.

"Give him another five or six years at this rate that we're going, oh my goodness. He's 25 and he's on 58! By the age of 30, he'll have 100 plus.

"Christian Wade is missing more tries per game than he is scoring tries but that probably shows where Newcastle's mindset is."

articles.title: Alex Lozowski: Saracens exit was sad and bewildering
articles.summary: Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was an anti-climax after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign.
articles.body:
Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was "sad" and "bewildering" after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign.

The 33-year-old England international made only two Prem appearances for Saracens last season, with a 10-minute Champions Cup cameo off the bench his only game time since the end of February.

"It was a sad ending for everyone I suppose," said Lozowski.

"They finished fifth, which is not where they wanted to be, and I wasn't part of it at all.

"It was probably just a bit of a damp squib at the end of the season really, which was a shame. It was bewildering and peculiar to me.

"They have their decisions and their reasons and, even though you can disagree with them as strongly as you like, it doesn't really count for much."

Lozowski, whose form in the 2024-25 season won him call-ups to England's squad for both the autumn internationals and Six Nations, was overlooked in favour of a midfield combination of Olly Hartley and Nick Tomkins for Saracens' run-in.

A streak of five successive victories took the London club to the brink of the play-offs before they lost away to Exeter in a semi-final shootout in the final round of the regular season.

"Sport teaches you all kinds of different lessons and now it's like a distant memory, but at the time it sort of stings," added Lozowski, who had a youth trial with Premier League side Arsenal and played for Chelsea's academy before being released and focusing on rugby.

"I've played 198 games, could have got a couple more in there and had a little run and tried to make it to the top four?' That's what I was thinking at the time, but it doesn't always work out the way you want."

Lozowski, who starts in Sale's midfield alongside fellow summer signing Joe Marchant at Saracens on Sunday, admits proving his value to his old club, along with spurring on his new side's season, will be part of his motivation.

"I know Sale wanted me to come here and add value, which meant a lot to me," he said.

Lozowski is not the only member of Sale's travelling party who will be in familiar surroundings at the Stonex Stadium.

Director of rugby Alex Sanderson spent 17 years at Saracens, initially as a player before working as a coach at the club.

Brendan Venter, who has returned to Saracens this season and already been fined for opting out of media appearances, was Sanderson's first boss as a coach.

"I idolised Brendan to a degree," he said.

"A lot of his traits, his values and philosophies I'm aligned with. I've taken from them over the years.

"Not withstanding Mark McCall's unbelievable contribution [who led Saracens for 15 years between Venter's stints], it's good to have him back in the Prem as a character. I'm sure we'll see his character come out on to the field."

Sale are seeking to avenge two heavy defeats against Saracens last season, going down 65-14 away from home in October, before an 85-16 thrashing in April's reverse fixture.

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Warrington and Wakefield battle to be winner number six
articles.summary: Only five clubs have lifted the trophy in a Super League Grand Final - Warrington and Wakefield now have the chance to add their name to that list.
articles.body:
Just five sides have lifted the trophy at Old Trafford in a Super League Grand Final.

That exclusive club of Wigan, Leeds, St Helens, Bradford and Hull KR will gain a new member on Saturday as Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity battle under the lights at the Theatre of Dreams for a spot at glory.

Whereas the Super League era has traditionally been dominated by the powerhouses of the sport with their heaving trophy cabinets, 2026 is the story of one side that has come close but not got over the line and another that has upset the odds to wedge themselves into the conversation.

But what is the mood like in either camp ahead of a box office Grand Final?

Wakefield eye repeat of Wigan performance

Wakefield's stunning semi-final win over Wigan set tongues wagging across rugby league and beyond, particularly given the nature of the demolition job delivered by Daryl Powell's side to the treble-chasers.

It was a performance which suggested Wakefield had the credentials to complete the job at Old Trafford, built on a marauding, metre-chomping pack and skilful, pacy backs capable of racking up points.

Head coach Powell has been around the block and knows just how difficult this one-off final is to get right even with a season's worth of momentum behind a team.

"We have to get the same performance level," Powell told BBC Sport. "When it really counts.

"I'm not saying it's going to be picture perfect, it's very rare there is but I think we have to be at a very high level to beat Warrington and we all know that."

'You could be legends' - inside unfancied Wakefield's rapid ascent

Will 2026 finally be Warrington Wolves' year?

Quiz: Name every Super League Grand Finalist

While this is Wakefield's first final and the same for many of their players, like coach Powell a select few have sampled the unique atmosphere of Old Trafford for Super League's showpiece event.

Tom Johnstone begrudgingly left Wakefield for Catalans in 2023 and reached the Grand Final in his first season, before rejoining Trinity in 2025.

That night ended in disappointment with defeat by Wigan, so the 2026 final represents a second chance for the England winger to pick up the ring he so covets - although it will not be the most important ring in his life as he admits.

"It's going to be different in so many ways for me because as much as I loved Catalans, this is my team," Johnstone told BBC Radio 5 live.

"This has been my team for almost all of my career, and the team that gave me an opportunity 15 years ago as a youngster.

"So, this is special, this is the big one and it's probably going to be, if we get it done, the best night of my life. Sorry, after my wedding, my wife said. She said it has to be second to my wedding."

Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield one win from title

Like Warrington, Wakefield have waited a long time to return to league glory, with a 58-year gap since their last title.

That narrative is one of many utilised by both clubs as inspiration for this Grand Final encounter, with several on both sides.

One story for Wakefield to thrive upon is the impending retirement of stalwart back-rower Jay Pitts.

Born in Ossett and a graduate of the youth set-up at Wakefield, the 36-year-old has amassed just short of 200 appearances for Trinity across two spells bookending his career which will end once Saturday's final is done.

Pitts has battled through this crucial period following a bicep injury, and his determination and leadership are integral to the spirit within the dressing room.

"After the Wigan game I just went into the changing rooms and said to him 'you know you get to play your final game at Old Trafford'. It's what dreams are made of," Powell added.

"While there's a few players leaving us for different reasons, for Pittsy retiring after his final game in rugby league - what better way for us all to do something special for him as a person?

"He's been a phenomenal player, a warrior, and I know all the boys love him. He gets a fair bit of stick for how old he is but that comes to us all so I won't worry about that too much."

It has been 71 years since Warrington last won a league title and it is their first trip to Old Trafford for eight years.

In the Super League era, the Wire have now reached five Grand Finals, but are yet to cross the line and write their name on the trophy.

For Ben Currie, he is acutely aware of the gap between trophies, having been with the club during their four other visits - albeit he is yet to actually a appear in a Grand Final.

"It's hard not to know about it when you've got the opposite fans singing about it every week," he told BBC Radio Merseyside.

"Obviously it's tongue in cheek and it's fun for the fans to do that.

"We'd love to give our fans the opportunity to sing back to them but there's no added pressure from anyone from above in the club, from the coaching staff or from the senior players.

"Everyone wants it just the same as everyone does at Wakefield."

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

One member of the Warrington team who could make an impact is 18-year-old Ewan Irwin.

Since making his debut in 2025, Irwin has gone on to make 21 appearances this season, scoring six tries and kicking 82 goals.

Matty Ashton, who himself was a bright young prospect for the Wire not so long ago, spoke highly of his team-mate, who has the chance to become the youngest player to ever score in a Grand Final.

"You see him day in and day out, his work ethic, he's probably the best I've seen in a young lad [and] obviously I've been at the club for seven years," Ashton said of Irwin to BBC Radio Merseyside.

"The way he's willing to learn when he speaks to leaders like George [Williams], it's just great to see.

"He's just got that something, you can see it. Obviously I don't want to put too much pressure as he's my team-mate, but he'll go all the way and he's got a big chance to do something like that."

Warrington name a squad with just one change in their line-up.

Jordy Crowther comes into the squad, with Max Wood dropping out.

Wakefield, meanwhile, are unchanged following their dramatic semi-final win against Wigan Warriors.

Josh Rourke is once again named in their provisional squad as he continues his return from a knee injury sustained in August.

articles.title: Cardiff 40-27 Zebre: Welsh side seal URC bonus-point victory against Italians
articles.summary: Cardiff continue their promising start to the United Rugby Championship (URC) with a six-try 40-27 home victory against Zebre.
articles.body:
Tries: T Williams, Sebastian, Basham, Mann, Bowen 2 Cons: Sheedy 4, Evans

Tries: Minervino, Ferrari, Bertaccini, Da Re Cons: Da Re 2 Pens: Allen

Cardiff continued their promising start to the United Rugby Championship (URC) campaign with a six-try home victory against Zebre.

Wing Tom Bowen crossed for two tries, with further scores from lock Teddy Williams, prop Javan Sebastian, number eight Taine Basham and flanker Alex Mann as Cardiff followed up their opening weekend victory against Scarlets.

Cardiff led 40-8 halfway through the second half but allowed Zebre, who lost 47-13 to Bulls in the opening round, back into the game as the Italian side scored three tries in the final 21 minutes.

Following a first-half try from hooker Francisco Minervino, Zebre's second-half revival provided scores for replacements Giacomo Ferrari and Giacomo Da Re, and centre Giulio Bertaccini.

The match was played in front of a crowd of 7,231 at the Arms Park, which was a similar attendance to that of the opening Welsh derby game between Scarlets and Cardiff in Llanelli.

Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup

Wales lock Williams back in Cardiff colours

Cardiff secure bonus point in first half

Cardiff made four personnel changes to the side that beat Scarlets , with hooker Dafydd Hughes and James Botham, who produced a player-of-the-match display, brought in for captain Liam Belcher and flanker Dan Thomas. Lock Josh McNally led the side in Belcher's absence.

Injured wing Mason Grady and full-back Cameron Winnett were ruled out as Harri Millard and Bowen were named on the wings and Jacob Beetham slotted in at full-back.

Zebre dominated the early exchanges with Italy international Tommaso Allan missing an easy penalty before slotting over the opening three points.

Cardiff rallied and after a flowing move, lock Williams powered over following a deft Mann try-scoring pass.

It was an ideal way for Williams to mark his first competitive home game for Cardiff after suffering a serious foot injury in October 2025 at the Arms Park.

The hosts extended the lead with a simple tap penalty move as Hughes released his front-row colleague Sebastian.

Zebre demonstrated a more clinical edge with Minervino driven over, but it did not take long for Cardiff to take control again.

Basham, who has enjoyed a barnstorming start to the season, made things look easy as his power and athleticism enabled him to crash over straight from an attacking scrum.

Cardiff were enjoying themselves and secured the bonus-point try in the 36th minute when Mann crossed to score.

A fizzing try-scoring pass from centre Ben Thomas and an outrageous Hughes dummy were the highlights in the build-up to the try as the hosts led 26-8 at half-time.

The main negative of the first half for Cardiff was prop Scott Sio being forced off because of injury.

Bowen at the double but Zebre bounce back

The second half started with some more ingenuity from fly-half Callum Sheedy, who last week went viral after heading the ball against Scarlets .

On this occasion, it was his clever grubber kick of a loose ball that went into the hands of Bowen, who skipped over.

Cardiff started the replacement process with hooker Evan Lloyd showing his versatility by covering the back row and coming on for Basham.

The stage was also set for 18-year-old hooker Tom Howe, who was introduced for his senior Cardiff debut.

The alterations did not halt Cardiff's momentum, initially, with Bowen sprinting over for his second score after being set up by scrum-half Johan Mulder.

Zebre had not given up hope, though, and gained some reward with scores for Ferrari and Bertaccini as the home side became increasingly sloppy.

The Italians secured a bonus-point try as they took advantage of Cardiff inexplicably losing concentration, with Da Re crossing following a searing break from full-back Giovanni Montemauri.

That proved the end of the scoring with Cardiff knowing there can be no repeat of this lacklustre final quarter when they travel to face defending champions Leinster in Dublin next Saturday.

articles.title: URC: Edinburgh 17-13 Stormers - hosts grind out victory
articles.summary: Edinburgh made it two wins from two in the United Rugby Championship with a gritty 17-13 home success against Stormers.
articles.body:
Tries: Hill, McHaffie Cons: Grayson 2 Pens: Grayson

Edinburgh made it two wins from two at the start of the United Rugby Championship season with a gritty success against Stormers at Hive Stadium.

The hosts were looking to continue the early-season momentum built with a superb bonus-point win away to Ulster last weekend.

South Africa captain Siya Kolisi was making his first appearance in a Stormers shirt in over five years, but it was Edinburgh who struck first with a long-range James Grayson penalty.

There was little to no action in either 22 in the first half, with dropped balls and the referee's whistle taking centre stage.

Stormers' attempts to make inroads into Edinburgh territory were repeatedly foiled by Liam McConnell, with the young flanker stealing three lineouts against the throw in the first half alone.

Magnus Bradbury thought he had crossed for the game's opening try just before half-time, but the referee judged he had made a double movement in the act of touching down and ruled it out.

Two penalties in three minutes early in the second half from Stormers fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed put the visitors in front as a strong breeze continued to impact the quality of attacking rugby from both sides.

The Stormers' lineout was wobbly throughout and it was their undoing as Edinburgh scored the opening try just before the hour mark.

A loose throw was picked off at the tail by Jerry Blyth-Lafferty, and a phase later the substitute hooker made a storming burst to take Edinburgh within inches of the South African line. They had a couple of cracks before another replacement, prop Paul Hill, dived over.

Wandisile Simelane thought he had wrestled the lead back for the visitors when he found his way to the line, but replays showed Piers O'Connor had done just enough to force the Stormers winger into touch before he touched down.

The reprieve was short-lived as a dominant Stormers scrum in the shadow of the posts allowed number eight Hacjivah Dayimani to peel off and power over.

The Edinburgh response was impressive. They battered at the Stormers line before swinging it wide to substitute Rory McHaffie. The 19-year-old did brilliantly to gather Grayson's pass off the deck and beat the cover defence to score on his home debut.

There was still work to do as Stormers kicked a penalty to the corner in the final play. Once again McConnell made a nuisance of himself at the lineout and disrupted the Stormers ball. It came back on the Edinburgh side and they were able to get it off the pitch to secure a hard-earned victory.

Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt told BBC Scotland: "It was a very hard-earned win.

"I'm just proud of the effort that they put in and the path that they showed at home. It shows that they care.

"A different opposition (from Ulster last weekend) against one of the best packs in the URC.

"Obviously, with the injuries that we had, we knew we had to contain their set-piece. I thought our boys were brave tonight and they stood up physically and, like I said, they showed they cared for the jersey.

"It's a great start for us. It's the total opposite to what we had last year.

"For these youngsters, I think we had 11 players 22 and under, getting one over those really good players that played for South Africa in the last month, I think it's great for us and it's going to build a lot of belief and sometimes that belief is more important than the league points."

articles.title: The Prem: Bath 40-34 Exeter: Bath beat Chiefs in 11-try thriller
articles.summary: After losing to Exeter at home in the Prem semi-final last season, Bath beat the Chiefs 40-34 in another thriller.
articles.body:
Tries: Redpath, van der Linde, du Preez, Russell, Penalty, Hill Cons: Russell 4

Tries: Varney, Yeandle, Iosefa-Scott, Feyi-Waboso 2 Cons: Slade 3 Pen: Skinner

Bath made it two wins out of two in the new Prem season as they gained a degree of revenge for losing to Exeter Chiefs in last season's semi-final.

The two sides produced another thrilling game, just as they did three months ago, exchanging 11 tries as the all-out attack approach to the new season continued.

The hosts scored four tries to have a bonus point in the bag by the break as Cameron Redpath, Bernard van der Linde, Dan du Preez and Finn Russell all scored to put them 26-10 ahead.

Stephen Varney and Jack Yeandle had got Exeter's first-half scores, before Josh Iosefa-Scott and two great tries from England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso turned the match on its head within 15 minutes of the restart.

But Varney gave up a penalty try for a deliberate knock-on and Ted Hill's effort took the game beyond their opponents, although Harvey Skinner kicked a late penalty to ensure the visitors came away from a second consecutive defeat with two bonus points.

The last meeting between the pair at the same venue is a match that will be remembered forever as the Chiefs came from 16 points down at half-time to win their Prem semi-final by a single point.

That defeat dethroned Bath as champions and they were looking ruthless as they grabbed two early tries.

Redpath read Skinner's intentions to make an interception at point-blank range, giving him a free run to the line from inside his own half and there was opportunism about Bath's second score, as scrum-half van der Linde spotted a gap, dummied and sprinted over from just outside the 22.

Exeter had to respond and Feyi-Waboso's burst near the corner drew in enough defenders to allow Varney to exploit space to get his side on the board.

However, they could not keep the hosts out for long with more livewire stuff from van der Linde at the heart of it as he combined with Ewan Richards and although the little South African was held up a few metres short, there was no stopping compatriot du Preez from that distance.

A simple maul from a line-out saw Chiefs hooker Yeandle dot it down for their second try, but Bath had their bonus point on half-time as they worked the ball back to Russell with a bit of space and the Scotland and Lions fly-half did the rest with a dummy, turn of pace and finish.

With Russell converting his own try, it left an identical half-time score to that sunny June afternoon and just as they did three months ago, Rob Baxter's side came storming back and within 15 minutes, they had turned a 16-point deficit into a five-point advantage.

A powerful drive by Kane James punctured a hole in Bath's defence with Iosefa-Scott eventually able to pick and go for the prop's second try in two games.

Then it was Feyi-Waboso's turn to come to the party as he cut a devastating line from outside to in after a huge floated pass from Skinner found him on the touchline.

And his second try arrived thanks to great support play after ex-Bath centre Will Butt danced his way through a gap in midfield to open up the game.

But unlike last time, Bath found a response as their reinforcements from the bench added grunt. Redpath spilled the ball with the line beckoning but as they kept the pressure on, Varney could not resist putting a hand out to stop a pass reaching Joe Cokanasiga and a try in the corner.

The penalty try was awarded and the Italy number nine sin-binned and with a man extra, replacement flanker Hill bulldozed his way to the line and with Russell adding the extras, they had more than a one-score cushion.

Henry Slade missed one penalty to reduce the gap to six points, but Skinner stepped up in the 79th minute from the 40-metre line as Exeter pragmatically made sure they collected a losing bonus point to go with one for scoring four tries, while Bath have a maximum 10 from their two opening wins.

'We'll be in a fight every single week' - reaction

Bath director of rugby Johann van Graan told BBC Radio Somerset:

" It was a crazy game of rugby once again, Bath versus Exeter. We started the game really well but then they came out punching after half-time and scored three unanswered tries.

"But then that's why this game is a 23-man effort as we then came back with the impact of our eight (subs) who made a really good difference, so I'm really happy with the five points.

"We're very proud of our bench and numbers 16 to 23 at this club are just as important as numbers one to 15."

Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Radio Devon:

"The important emotion is I'm walking away going 'we've got a team here and we've got something to work with'.

"Last week was such a patchy performance ( losing 45-24 to Gloucester ) but today we showed a lot of good qualities.

"The qualities of being in a fight to the death, that's what Exeter Chiefs are about. Do you want to be perfect or do you want to be in a fight every single week? Well we'll be in a fight every single week.

"I'm quite happy with that, that's what we're good at and I saw that today."

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Bath beat Exeter Chiefs in pulsating West Country derby to move top of table
articles.summary: Bath climb to top of table after claiming derby honours in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec; they avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat to Exeter in another thriller
articles.body:
Exeter trailed 26-10 at the interval but rallied to lead 33-31 midway through the second half before a yellow card for scrum-half Stephen Varney eventually proved decisive.

Cam Redpath, Dan du Preez, Bernard van der Linde, Ted Hill and Finn Russell scored Bath's tries. There was also a penalty try award with Russell converting four.

The hugely impressive Immanuel Feyi-Waboso scored two tries for Exeter with Jack Yeandle, Josh Iosefa-Scott and Varney also going over. Henry Slade converted three and Harvey Skinner added a late penalty.

Bath took control as first Redpath intercepted a Skinner pass to run 50 metres and score before Van der Linde slipped through a gap in the visitors' defence for an individual try. Russell converted both to give his side a 14-0 lead at the end of the first quarter.

Exeter badly needed a response and they got one thanks to the strong running of Feyi-Waboso. First he evaded a tackle from Ollie Lawrence to put the defence on the back foot and when the ball was recycled he powered past another two coverers with Varney on hand to touchdown.

The hosts scored their third try when a favourable bounce on halfway saw them capitalise with Van der Linde and Ewan Richards taking advantage to give Du Preez the chance to force his way over from close range but Bath bungled the kick-off so Yeandle was able to keep his side in contention with a try from a driving lineout.

However with half-time approaching, Bath exerted a period of pressure culminating in Russell dummying his way over for the bonus-point try before converting for a 26-10 interval lead.

Exeter began the second half strongly and were rewarded with two tries in quick succession. First Iosefa-Scott crashed over from close range before Feyi-Waboso took his opportunity in style by brushing aside two would-be tacklers. Slade converted both and his side were right back in the contest with just two points between the teams.

Exeter took the lead for the first time when former Bath man Will Butt carved the hosts apart to provide Feyi-Waboso with an easy run-in for his second try.

The home side were soon awarded a penalty try with Varney yellow-carded for a deliberate knock-on and in the scrum-half's absence, Hill battered his way over the tryline.

Slade missed badly with a penalty attempt so Skinner took over the goal-kicking and his success gave Chiefs two deserved bonus points from the match.

articles.title: 10 injured after car crashes into rugby supporters in Australia
articles.summary: New South Wales police say the driver, an 18-year-old rugby league fan, has been arrested.
articles.body:
A car has crashed into a crowd of rugby league supporters in the eastern Australian city of Newcastle, injuring 10 people, including three children.

New South Wales police said on Saturday that two of the injured – a five-year-old girl and a 67-year-old man – were in a critical condition and the other eight were in stable condition in hospital.

Police said they had arrested the 18-year-old man driving the vehicle and were investigating what happened. They said the crash was not believed to be related to terrorism.

The crowd had gathered to farewell the local rugby league side, the Newcastle Knights, ahead of their grand final against the Sydney Roosters on Sunday.

Newcastle Lord Mayor Gavin Morris said the driver, a rugby league fan, had lost control of his vehicle and had been taken into custody.

“He was revving the car, he was excited, he was a supporter, he was there for the joy of the moment,” Morris told the national broadcaster ABC.

“Somehow he lost control of the car … and he’s gone into the crowd,” he added.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said: “My thoughts are with everyone injured or involved in the horrible incident this morning in Newcastle.”

“Rugby league brings people together, and this should have been a weekend of excitement and pride for Newcastle fans,” he wrote in a social media post.

articles.title: Worcestershire woman fought to get menopause diagnosis for years
articles.summary: Sally Williams says she wants other women to be aware of the "danger zone" of perimenopause.
articles.body:
For three years, Sally Williams struggled to understand what was happening to her as her mental health deteriorated and her life fell apart, spending almost 11 months in hospital across eight admissions.

She left her finance job, was separated from her teenage son and found herself fighting for her life, unaware her symptoms could be linked to perimenopause.

"No one joined the dots," Williams said. "It was only me... I joined the dots and it was transformational to start hormone replacement therapy and literally come back to life."

Williams, who initially self-diagnosed, wants other women to be aware of perimenopause, the years leading up to menopause, which she described as the "danger zone".

Perimenopause , which commonly begins around the age of 46, is when women experience menopause symptoms while still having periods.

Symptoms can include anxiety, mood swings, brain fog, hot flushes and irregular periods, with some women taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to help alleviate the symptoms.

What is the menopause and what are the main signs?

How does Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) work?

When her symptoms began in her late 40s, Williams, from the Wychavon area, said doctors she saw initially thought she had depression.

"I had multiple attempts on my life, two significant ones, one where I was in a wheelchair for three months for polytrauma, and this was in Covid, so there were no visitors. I had no contact with anyone," she explained.

"I had to leave my job. This was at perimenopause time. My message to women is that, menopause is not the danger zone, it's the run up, it's the 45 to 54."

For Williams, who said she was "unrecognisable" before her eventual diagnosis, it was HRT which eventually helped her, but she said it may not be for everyone.

The drug , which isn't suitable for some women, tops up and stabilises oestrogen levels, sometimes in combination with a synthetic or bioidentical version of progesterone.

Williams is set to speak about her hard fought menopause diagnosis at Meno Fest at Worcester Rugby Club on 7 October , as part of Menopause Awareness Month.

The free event is being held with the aim of helping people to gain greater understanding of how perimenopause and menopause can affect every aspect of life from physical and mental health to relationships, work and family life.

Williams told the BBC of how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause.

"I lost my job. I didn't see my friends, my family for three years and I was a recluse. I was self neglecting. And my son, who was in his teens, I probably saw him three times," she explained.

"He had leave his school and his friends and he had to go and live with his dad because he couldn't see me. I couldn't care for him."

It was also important that men recognised what was happening to women during perimenopause, she added.

"I think men need to come into the conversation as well, and I'm not just talking husbands and partners, I'm talking sons," she said.

"It was devastating and there's relationships that have been broken that will never be put back together. I'm very sad about that."

If you have been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line .

articles.title: Henry Slade: Exeter boss Rob Baxter backs centre after missed kicks at Bath
articles.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter urges Henry Slade not to dwell on his missed kicks in their loss at Bath.
articles.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter has urged Henry Slade not to dwell on his missed kicks in their loss at Bath.

Slade missed two first-half conversions before hitting the post with a penalty late in the second half as Chiefs went down 40-34 in a thrilling game at the Rec.

Team-mate Harvey Skinner stepped up to kick a 79th-minute penalty for Exeter that secured a losing bonus point as Baxter's side search for a first win of the season.

"I think we've been very fortunate with Henry over the years, but particularly last year," Baxter told BBC Radio Devon as Slade practised kicks after the final whistle.

"You think how many clutch kicks in big games he's knocked over for us and kept us in games, pushed us through things and just taking those real pressure kicks and he's always stood up and done it. You know there's going to be the odd game.

"But the most important thing for him is he shakes it off.

"I'd rather he wasn't out here practising now and he just goes and sits and has a beer and chills out because I don't think this is the way for him to get out of his system.

"But I'll have a chat with him as I walk past now and tell him to get in there and enjoy being with the lads, because he's too good a player for this to be an issue."

Bath gain revenge on Exeter to win 11-try thriller

Exeter reached last season's Prem final, where they lost to Northampton at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

But they have yet to record a win this season after a surprising loss at home to Gloucester last week.

Baxter says his side's loss at Bath, and their sticky start to the season, should not cause too much concern yet.

"In a way, I'll be worried that we think we have to get five points second game of the season to be competitive," he said.

"What I want us to do is go, 'We play really well every week, we build our points score', that's what gets us where we need to be.

"We saw that last year - that's what we've got to do again."

articles.title: Ireland v Japan: Hosts secure comprehensive win over visitors
articles.summary: Ireland secure a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan in their international Test at Virgin Media Park in Cork.
articles.body:
Tries: Cahill, Hogan, Jones, McGann, Parsons, McInerney, Barrett Cons: O'Brien 2, Breen 2

Tries: Korai, Asari, Nagata Cons: Nishi 2

Ireland scored seven tries as they secured a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan in their Test match at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday.

Scott Bemand's side had defeated the same opponents in a WXV Global Series encounter in Galway the previous weekend.

Ireland recovered from conceding an early try to cross the whitewash four times in the first half to help them to a 22-7 advantage at the break.

Japan rallied but the hosts extended their lead in the second period to ensure they travel to face South Africa for a two-match series in the WXV with confidence high and momentum gathered.

Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett both marked their debuts off the bench with tries.

Ireland had begun their series of autumn matches with a disappointing 40-36 defeat by the USA at Tallaght Stadium but recovered to beat Japan 31-24 in Galway.

The opening minutes of Saturday's contest were marked by a high penalty count on the part of Ireland and Japan took full advantage of their indiscipline as Sakurako Korai barged over from close range after just five minutes.

Emily Lane dotted down soon after but the score was ruled out for an infringement in the build-up.

Prop Eilis Cahill powered over after Ireland worked the ball well through the phases, with Dannah O'Brien's conversion levelling the scores.

Masami Kawamura was sin-binned for cynical play in holding up an attack and Ireland made use of their numerical advantage when Brittany Hogan rumbled over to build on her double try-scoring appearance last week.

Sustained pressure from the home side resulted in two further touchdowns before the interval.

Neve Jones crashed over after some enterprising play and another huge maul effort and then Anna McGann showed strength to stretch and ground the ball after Niamh Gallagher broke through and Erin King provided the pass.

Just two minutes after the resumption, Beibhinn Parsons rode a tackle and went over after a flowing move through the hands as she extended her all-time record of Ireland tries to 25.

Parsons accelerated and dotted down over the try-line, with O'Brien adding the extras.

Teenager Nami Asari led something of a Japan fightback as patient play culminated in her scoring for the second week in a row.

Nijiho Nagata crashed over from another maul to reduce the deficit to 10 but the away side's momentum was halted when Nishi was yellow-carded for head-to-head contact on King.

McInerney shrugged off a couple of attempted tackles and dived over beside the upright after being introduced off the bench.

Then, as the clock ticked into the red, it was the turn of fellow debutant Barrett to pick up and dive across the line for try number seven for her side.

Enya Breen's conversion put 24 points between the teams at the final whistle.
