articles.title: Dragons celebrate derby success against Scarlets
articles.summary: Dragons secure a Welsh derby win in a United Rugby Championship (URC) 10-try thrilling encounter at Rodney Parade in Newport.
articles.body:
Tries: Tuitavuki, Dee 2 , Martinez, Anderson, Hunt Cons: de Beer 3 , J Lloyd

Tries : Page 2 , S O'Connor, I Jones Cons: Costelow 3

Dragons secured a Welsh derby win in the United Rugby Championship (URC), beating Scarlets in a thrilling 10-try encounter at Rodney Parade.

Two tries from Wales hooker Elliot Dee,and further scores from wing Anzelo Tuitavuki, props Rodrigo Martinez and Rob Hunt and full-back Huw Anderson sealed the six-try success.

Scarlets responded with two tries from wing Macs Page and scores from replacements Sam O'Connor and Ioan Jones.

The match was played in front of a raucous crowd of 7,163 that created a memorable occasion in Newport.

Dragons are unbeaten, following up the opening weekend draw with Benetton, while Scarlets, who are missing influential injured back-row duo Taine Plumtree and Fletcher Anderson, have suffered two derby defeats, having also lost at home to Cardiff.

Scarlets score first as they lead at half-time

Wales fly-half Sam Costelow was among five personnel changes from the Scarlets team that lost 21-15 defeat to Cardiff, with Wales props Kemsley Mathias and Harri O'Connor, lock Alex Groves and flanker Dan Davis starting.

Dragons co-captain Ben Carter returned to lead the side that drew 19-19 with Benetton , but fellow skipper Angus O'Brien was still missing.

Dee, Hunt, and back-row duo Shane Lewis-Hughes and Harri Keddie were also included.

Scrum-half Rhodri Williams led the side out with his family on his 150th Dragons appearance against his former team, where he spent five seasons.

The two teams ran out to easily the most fervent atmosphere of a Welsh home match so far this season, with the fixture benefiting from its sunny Saturday afternoon kick-off time.

It was the away fans who were celebrating first as Page scored a superb solo try after drifting around the Dragons defence before collecting his own chip.

The hosts responded with a period of pressure that was rewarded with a first Dragons try for Tongan wing Tuitavuki.

This inspired the hosts as they kept up the pressure with a well-worked line-out between centre Aneurin Owen and flanker Thomas Young, which laid the platform for another attacking set-piece that yielded a driving try for Dee.

Scarlets scrum-half Dane Blacker sought to install some tempo in the visitors' play, and an attacking scrum allowed centre Eddie James to burst through the middle, before a long Costelow floated pass released Page to stroll in for his second.

Costelow converted as Scarlets led 14-12 at half-time.

Dragons dominate second half to seal win

Dragons struck straight after the break when wing Rio Dyer took the ball superbly from kick-off to put the hosts on the front foot.

After subtle build-up work from de Beer and Anderson, a searing Tuitavuki break was only halted by a brilliant tap tackle from Scarlets full-back Blair Murray, but Argentina prop Martinez followed up to cross, with de Beer converting.

Scarlets retaliated and, following another midfield charge from James, a perfect Page chip narrowly eluded Mee's hands as he lost possession over the Dragons line.

The home side brought on Wales props Rhodri Jones and Dillon Lewis as the duo forced a scrum penalty.

Scarlets replacement prop Sam O'Connor made his own early impression when he burrowed over for the third try.

Costelow's conversion regained the lead, but Scarlets put themselves under pressure with needless penalties from the kick-off.

Dragons flanker Young was held up over the line but it was Anderson who scored the bonus-point try in the right-hand corner to give the Dragons the advantage once more.

Dyer produced an excellent break, and Scarlets captain Josh Macleod could only stop the momentum with a professional foul that resulted in a yellow card.

The hosts took control with Dee driven over for his second score, which proved his final act before being replaced.

Scarlets, playing with 14 men, struck back quickly with a quick line-out before replacement Jones crossed for the bonus-point try.

Dragons gathered themselves and Hunt's final try sealed the success in what was a fourth try on the day for the home front-row.

Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia: "We had all the possession and territory in the first half but just weren't clinical enough.

"We were in control and needed to maximise the opportunities when they were on.

"I am proud of the group. We want to keep growing and keep going up the ladder."

articles.title: The Prem: Bristol 34-26 Northampton: Bristol get revenge on reigning champions
articles.summary: Louis Rees-Zammit scores a double as Bristol edge past reigning champions Northampton in a pulsating Prem tussle.
articles.body:
Tries: Oghre, Rees-Zammit 2, Jordan, Randall, Penalty Cons: Williams 3 Pens: Williams

Tries: Hendy 2, Mitchell, Kemeny Cons: F. Smith 3

Louis Rees-Zammit scored a double as Bristol Bears edged past reigning champions Northampton Saints in a pulsating Prem tussle at Ashton Gate.

Although defences were on top in the first half and chances were limited, the tactical battle and ruthless finishing provided great entertainment as they ran in two tries apiece.

Gabriel Oghre opened the scoring for the hosts following a well-worked line-out move and maul before George Hendy crossed in the corner.

And, after Rees-Zammit's clinical close-range score, Hendy went over again to leave the match finely poised at 15-14 in Bristol's favour at the break.

Unanswered, converted tries from Tom Jordan and Harry Randall gave Bears significant breathing space at 29-14, only for two tries in four minutes from Alex Mitchell and Josh Kemeny to get Saints back in the game at 34-26.

But Bears managed to blunt the Saints attack in the closing stages and sealed the win in the final seconds with a penalty try, awarded after a cynical intervention by Saints full-back Tommy Freeman denied Rees-Zammit a hat-trick.

Bath gain revenge on Exeter to win 11-try thriller

MacGinty savouring Bristol return after long spell out

Following an emotional tribute and minute's applause for Jackie Booy, who died last month, led by her husband and Bristol chairman Chris, Bears set about marking the occasion in fitting fashion with a stylish display that combined, brilliant defence and scintillating attack.

Oghre's set-piece score gave Bears, who were unceremoniously thrashed 94-33 by Saints last season, a sixth-minute lead that was soon wiped out by Hendy's dart to the corner following a fine set-piece move and pass by captain Fraser Dingwall.

A James Williams penalty restored the lead for the Bears, who then had a sumptuous score ruled out, Randall knocking on in the build up to AJ MacGinty's fine cross kick after great work by Rees-Zammit on the right.

However, Bristol speedster Rees-Zammit's next contribution counted, the winger skipping home into the corner from close range to put his side 15-7 to the good.

But, after a lengthy delay following a nasty looking head injury to Bristol's new England international Benhard Janse van Rensburg, the visitors reduced the half-time deficit to a point when Smith's perfectly timed pass out wide allowed Hendy to double his and his side's first-half try tally.

Thankfully, Janse van Rensburg was up and walking around during the break, but his absence did not knock Bears out of their stride on their way to a second successive Prem victory this season.

Tom Jordan stretched over to touch down for the third home try soon after the restart and Williams slotted his third kick of the afternoon to make it 22-14.

A third Saints try was then disallowed following an obstruction, and the sniping Randall then bundled over for a converted try near the posts to further extend the home side's advantage after the Saints defence were sucked in to keep the Bears at bay on the line.

Northampton's quality in attack, showcased so stylishly in their nine-try mauling of Newcastle last time out, could not be contained for long with two tries in four minutes putting them within eight points of their hosts.

A slick move saw Dingwall feed Hendy, who selflessly teed up Mitchell on the inside to go under the posts and Kemeny's try put the visitors within eight points.

Bristol showed no signs of panic as their defence held firm impressively to close out a victory sealed with a last-gasp penalty try.

Bristol director rugby Pat Lam told BBC Radio Bristol:

"We are very pleased. It's more evidence for the players of the unseen work they are putting in.

"We always get recognised for the tries but finally the forwards are getting some recognition for the work they do up front.

"We really challenged their ball carriers and speed of ruck.

"We had a moment when they were coming back but we turned that tide. I am really proud of these guys because we had a physical game against Sale last week. For the boys to through it again - against the champions at full strength - is massive

"We are disappointed to give them a bonus point but we are pleased we didn't give them a second bonus point."

Bristol director rugby Phil Dowson told BBC Radio Northampton:

"It's very disappointing. We can't seem to get it right at Ashton Gate. We weren't good enough in lots of facets of our game. That's a really good indication of where we are at the moment.

"Bristol were excellent. They worked really hard at the breakdown and we didn't deal with it.

"It's early in the season and that tells us where we need to train. The game doesn't lie. We are not firing on all cylinders in some aspects.

"But we don't get too high after a win or too low after a loss. We must learn as quickly as possible so we can get better."

articles.title: The Prem: Gloucester 48-0 Harlequins: Cherry and Whites thrash pointless Quins
articles.summary: Gloucester thrash a limp Harlequins at Kingsholm to go to the top of the early Prem standings.
articles.body:
Tries: Loader, Morgan, Trenholm, C. Atkinson, S. Atkinson, Englefield, Joseph, Barton Cons: Barton 4

Gloucester thrashed a limp Harlequins at Kingsholm to go to the top of the early Prem standings.

The Cherry and Whites ran in eight tries to make it two wins from two in the league and three on the bounce in all competitions.

Gloucester, who named three new signings in their starting line-up including Wales internationals Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, completely outplayed their opponents in all facets of the match.

Visitors Quins, who handed a debut to England full-back George Furbank, struggled to get a handle on the game from the outset and remain bottom of the table without any points after failing to get on the scoreboard.

Rees-Zammit stars as Bristol power past Northampton

Gloucester winger Cokanasiga out until January

A progressive move down the right gave Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson – three days after he signed a new deal committing his long-term future with the club - the opportunity to find Ben Loader free on the left with a pinpoint kick, and the winger dotted down to open the scoring.

Harlequins, in their desperation to keep Gloucester out on their own try line, lost Will Evans to the sin bin and mere seconds later Wales flanker Morgan barged over in the left corner to extend Gloucester's lead.

On the stroke of half hour, Morgan's strong carry allowed Will Trenholm to force over Gloucester's third try from close range before George Barton slotted the conversio superbly from touch.

A spectacular 50:22 from scrum-half Caolan Englefield then put Gloucester in another great position and Charlie Atkinson broke a tackle to go over next to the sticks, as Barton kicked an easy extra two to give the hosts a 24-point advantage at half-time.

The interval did not change the momentum as two short passes saw Seb Atkinson race to the line and power over Gloucester's fifth of the evening and Quins' day was perhaps summed up best when Connor Slevin's poor restart failed to go 10 metres.

Gloucester ruthlessly made their visitors pay once more as with their next attack Will Joseph's outstanding run and offload allowed Englefield to dive over.

Joseph then grabbed the try his own performance deserved, diving in to the right of the posts to claim Gloucester's seventh try and third inside 12 minutes after half-time.

Another kick to the corner from Charlie Atkinson found Barton who juggled successfully and managed to extend over for Gloucester's eighth.

Joseph thought he had scored his second with the final act of the match to take Gloucester past 50 points, but his try was chalked off for a knock-on in the build up.

'Outstanding' and 'totally unacceptable' - reaction

Gloucester head coach George Skivington told BBC Radio Gloucestershire:

"I expected us to be good in defence, I expected us to try and back up what we did last week but nilling a team is outstanding and that shows character more than anything.

"The work Joel Tomkins [defence coach] has done to get the boys in that mindset is great.

"The snapshot for me of the game is when we are winning at the end and we chase back as hard as we did to stop Quins getting a try - that's really the character we're looking for.

"All round pretty happy, I think there's a lot of things we can do better. We felt like that at half-time, that was what we talked about, and that's testament to the group - they're working unbelievably hard, theyre not satisfied."

Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore said:

"The performance was totally unacceptable and you are not going to win a game with a 21-5 penalty count against you.

"We fed the referee, which meant we struggled for possession, and they were able to get easy field position and were able to launch 20 line-outs in the red zone to our five.

"At half-time we felt we could still do something but conceding two tries in the first four minutes after the interval took the wind out of our sails.

"That put the result beyond doubt and we spun out of control afterwards as we tried to chase the game."

articles.title: Glasgow Warriors 33-33 Ulster: Thrilling Scotstoun draw in United Rugby Championship
articles.summary: George Horne's late penalty hits the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster play out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship.
articles.body:
Tries: McKay, Rowe 2, Dobie,Talakai Cons: Horne 4

Tries: B Ward, McIlroy, Murphy, Mullins, Augustus Cons: Murphy 3, Doak

George Horne's late penalty hit the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster played out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship.

Ulster, seeking their first win in Glasgow in more than five years, led 19-14 at the break but the Warriors scored three tries in a clinical nine-minute spell when Ulster had two players sin-binned to take the lead.

But Glasgow were reduced to 13 inside the final 10 minutes and Juarno Augustus' try, converted by Nathan Doak, levelled the game.

Despite being two players down, Horne had a chance to win the match but his penalty came back off the upright with four minutes left and the points were shared at Scotstoun.

There was blow for Ulster before kick-off as Jacob Stockdale, set to win his 150th cap, was forced out of the starting team in the warm-up but the visitors did not let his withdrawal impact their start.

After being slow out of the blocks at home to Edinburgh in their opener proved costly, Ulster started the better side and took the lead when Bryn Ward barrelled over the line in the fourth minute from a short penalty, and Jack Murphy converted.

Glasgow Warriors draw with Ulster in URC - as it happened

But Glasgow, who only lost at home once in the entirety of last season, hit back when Josh McKay rounded off a flowing move, and George Horne added the conversion to level the game.

That handed the Warriors the momentum but the hosts were soon reduced to 14 players when Dan Lancaster was sent to the sin-bin for a deliberate knock on, and Ulster immediately capitalised when Ethan McIlroy darted through a gap to score after building pressure on the home line.

Glasgow responded when Kyle Rowe crossed after a superb pass by centre Stafford McDowall, which took three Ulster players out of the game, and Horne converted to put the hosts into a two-point lead.

There was a final twist in the half when Horne won a penalty after being dragged into a ruck but retaliated by throwing the ball at Ulster hooker Tom Stewart, and the decision was reversed.

Ulster went up the other end and McIlroy's superb offload allowed Murphy to cross in the final play of the half.

The fly-half converted his own score to give Ulster a five-point lead at the break.

Chay Mullins marked his debut by scoring Ulster's bonus-point try just six minutes after the restart after more good work from McIlroy, and Murphy's conversion put the visitors 12 points clear.

But indiscipline cost Ulster as Ben Carson, who was drafted into the team to replace Stockdale, was sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on McDowall and, in the following play, McIlroy was also carded for a deliberate knock on to leave Richie Murphy's side with 13 players.

Glasgow immediately took advantage as Jamie Dobie raced over in the corner after the hosts worked some space, and Horne landed his third conversion of the game.

The hosts were held up over the line from a rolling maul, but they made the most of their momentum when Sam Talakai burrowed over the line to level the game, and Horne nudged Glasgow back in front.

Despite having Carson back on the field, Rowe then raced clear to extend Glasgow's lead after some soft Ulster defence.

But Rory Darge and Talakai were sent to the sin bin inside the final 10 minutes to leave the hosts with 13 after repeated infringements as Ulster camped on the Glasgow line, and Augustus crashed over before Doak levelled the game.

In late drama, Carson was penalised for holding on at a ruck to give Glasgow a kickable penalty but Horne could only hit the upright.

The final minutes were chaotic as both sides threw away possession in search of a decisive score, but Zac Ward was bundled into touch with the clock in the red to ensure the game ended level.

Glasgow Warriors host Connacht on Friday in their third match of the season while Ulster face Munster in Belfast on Saturday.

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Warrington Wolves 10-23 Wakefield Trinity - Trinity claim Grand Final success
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity end a 58-year wait to be champions as they claim a deserved Grand Final success over Warrington Wolves at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Tries: Scott, Vagana, Tevaga, Johnstone Goals: Jowitt 3 Drop goal: Sinfield

Wakefield Trinity became only the sixth, and most unlikely, club to win the Super League title after a deserved win over Warrington Wolves.

Only two years after being in the Championship and in their first ever Grand Final, Wakefield took to the Old Trafford stage as if they were to the manor born.

Daryl Powell's side did the bulk of the damage in a devastating first half as they raced into a 19-0 lead on their way to becoming champions of England for the first time since 1968, long before the Super League era.

Trinity carried on from where they had left off in the semi-final against Wigan Warriors with tries from Cameron Scott, Isaiah Vagana and Jazz Tevaga and a drop goal from Jack Sinfield.

Arron Lindop's try gave Warrington brief hope early in the second half, but when Tom Johnstone went over at the other end, the game was up despite Lindop's second try late on.

This is a final few would have predicted seven days ago, let alone at any point throughout the season.

But Warrington snuck past Leeds Rhinos, and Wakefield Trinity then stunned the whole of rugby league as they demolished Wigan on the Warriors' own patch to make it to Old Trafford.

While Warrington have been close in previous years, Wakefield have been spectacular bolters in 2026.

Only two years ago, they were winning the Championship play-off final before their place in Super League was confirmed by the IMG grading system, having been relegated in 2023.

They were sixth last year and went two places better this season before memorable play-off successes over Leigh Leopards and then the Warriors.

In the build-up during the week, Powell had challenged his players to earn legendary status , knowing that was their long-term reward if they could emerge victorious.

After scoring 33 unanswered points in a spell at Wigan, Wakefield simply brought that momentum with them to Old Trafford as they absolutely bossed the first half, stretching that streak to 52 points.

Johnstone had already had one try denied by a TV review before Lachlan Walmsley's brilliant reverse pass sent Scott over to score.

And in a period where everything they did was working, Jake Trueman's high kick on the last tackle was spectacularly caught by Johnstone above opposite wing Albert Hopoate and tapped back for the supporting Vagana to dive over.

They were overpowering their opponents, exemplified by Tevaga being unstoppable from close to the posts for their third try.

And showing the sort of game smarts his revered father Sir Kevin Sinfield had in his Leeds Rhinos days, son Jack added an extra point to keep the scoreboard ticking as the half closed to leave Warrington needing more than three converted tries.

In the Super League era, Warrington have been the eternal bridesmaids, watching on as traditional rivals Wigan and St Helens have swept up the silverware.

This was their fifth Grand Final, and felt like the chance to finally get their hands on the big prize and be champions for the first time since 1955.

Under head coach Sam Burgess, they had lost Challenge Cup finals at Wembley in the previous two years, but they had arrived at this game on the back of nine wins out of 10.

Crucially that sole defeat had been at Wakefield in round 26 of the regular season and in the opening 40 minutes, they had few answers.

But a high tackle by Trinity centre Corey Hall resulted in him being sin-binned early in the second period and, with a man extra, Lindop went over to offer a glimmer of a comeback.

However, Warrington could not score again with that momentum. Wakefield weathered the storm and, with numbers levelled up, they worked an opening for Johnstone's power and pace to deliver the decisive try.

Lindop went over again for his second as the Wolves desperately attacked, but with Ewan Irwin missing the conversion, Trinity players and staff were able to count down until the final whistle before celebrations could begin as Warrington's wait for another title now extends to a 72nd year.

articles.title: The Prem: Newcastle 19-24 Leicester - Tigers pick up first win of season.
articles.summary: Leicester Tigers pick up their first win of the season with a tense and hard-fought victory at Newcastle Red Bulls in the Prem.
articles.body:
Tries: Ene, McGuigan, Jordan Cons: Connon, Henry

Tries: Moli, Radwan, Hurd Cons: Searle 3 Pens: Searle

Leicester Tigers picked up their first win of the season with a tense and hard-fought victory at Newcastle Red Bulls.

Former Newcastle winger Adam Radwan scored on his return to Kingston Park as the Tigers won for the first time in seven matches in all competitions, following a dismal run which stretches back into last season.

After being edged out by two points in a high-scoring thriller by Saracens six days ago, Leicester had to show their grit and determination to cling on to victory against a Newcastle side who threatened a late comeback.

Newcastle took the lead through Obi Ene's early score but, despite putting in a positive showing, they ultimately came up just short in their first home match of the season.

Gloucester thrash sorry Quins to go top of the Prem

Rees-Zammit stars as Bristol power past Northampton

Wade closes in on record as tries dominate Prem

Ene scored three minutes into his Prem debut after Newcastle moved the ball left. The former Sale winger weaved inside, having collected fly-half Brett Connon's excellent cut-out pass, to dive over for the opener.

But Leicester hit back when hooker Samiuela Moli launched himself over at the back of a driving maul and Billy Searle popped over the conversion to give Tigers a slender advantage.

Gabriel Hamer-Webb had an opportunity to go over for Leicester soon after but was pushed into touch by an excellent try-saving tackle from Christian Wade, before Hamer-Webb made his own outstanding score-stopping challenge as Newcastle's Harrison Obatoyinbo threatened to break clear.

That moment proved to be pivotal as former Newcastle winger Radwan latched on to Freddie Steward's exquisite grubber kick to touch down. After Searle kicked the conversion, the fly-half then added a penalty in front of the sticks.

Newcastle missed two presentable opportunities to score a second try before half-time and the match restarted in a scrappy manner after the break - until Ene was prevented from scoring a second try of the match thanks to a textbook challenge from Leicester replacement Will Wand.

Radwan spurned a good opportunity to score his second, kicking the ball dead when he had a whole half of the field to run into. Leicester were made to pay for their profligacy when George McGuigan's pick-and-go enabled him to drive over from close range to help pull the deficit back to five points.

Leicester got a vital third try of the night when Will Hurd's quick tap let him barrel over, and Searle kicked the conversion to make it a two-score game once more with 12 minutes remaining.

Newcastle carved through Leicester with just under seven minutes left when Ollie Leatherbarrow's bold carry saw him break a tackle as Cameron Jordan went over with Zack Henry adding the extras.

With the clock ticking down, Wade carried Newcastle forward with a trademark burst down the wing, but the home side were eventually guilty of holding on as Leicester gratefully kicked to touch to claim victory.

'We were not accurate enough' - reaction

Newcastle Red Bulls director of rugby Dan McFarland told BBC Radio Newcastle:

"I'm really disappointed, to be honest. It was a game we could have won. Really pleased with the way we approached the game. I thought we were full of effort, full of energy.

"Most importantly, we were full of the endeavour that we wanted to put in, in terms of the way we wanted to play the game.

"Unfortunately, we were not accurate enough in key areas - but that will grow.

"We are trying not to play in a boring way. Today, we weren't where we wanted to be. In the first half, we gave away penalties at set-piece and let them into our 22. I thought we improved in that area as the game went on."

Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling told BBC Radio Leicester:

"Gritty and dogged. Defensively, some good resolve and they're [Newcastle] going to break some teams this year with their quality attack and good speed.

"You go all pre-season and you try to build some real cohesion and you lose a lot of guys in the same position, but no excuses, we've just got to be better. I've got to help those guys to be able to execute in those moments.

"There's loads to improve on. The general feeling in the changing room is disappointment, which is great for me.

"Accuracy in the second half, especially at set-piece, we didn't allow ourselves to build up some pressure."

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Louis Rees-Zammit scores two tries as Bristol Bears beat champions Northampton Saints
articles.summary: Bristol lay down a marker as they beat Gallagher Prem champions Northampton 41-26 with Louis Rees-Zammit scoring twice; in an abject performance Harlequins lose 48-0 to Gloucester; Leicester beat Newcastle 24-19
articles.body:
Rees-Zammit followed up his two tries against opening opponents Sale Sharks with another double to put Bristol on the way to a bonus-point success.

He also shone in defence as Bristol largely nullified Northampton's free-flowing game, while Harry Randall, Gabriel Oghre and Tom Jordan added further Bristol tries, and there was also a penalty try, with James Williams kicking three conversions and a penalty.

Northampton trailed by just a point at half-time and were in contention throughout but they ultimately came up short despite scores from George Hendy (2), Alex Mitchell and Josh Kemeny, while Fin Smith booted three conversions. Saints finished with 13 players following yellow cards for Tommy Freeman and Ion Neculai.

Rees-Zammit's second touchdown took Bristol past 30 points, yet Northampton served a reminder that they were not quite out of it through substitute Mitchell's score 16 minutes from time that Smith converted before Kemeny scored and further ruffled the home team.

Bristol, though, had done enough to make it two wins from two in the Prem and set themselves up for an appointment with Saracens next time out, sealing it through a penalty try following an illegal challenge from Freeman on Rees-Zammit.

Gloucester continued their impressive start to the Gallagher Prem season by handing out a 48-0 thrashing to hapless Harlequins at Kingsholm.

The eight-try win followed up their impressive opening-day victory over Exeter at Sandy Park - but that success was far more meritorious as Harlequins were incredibly poor on the day.

Quins were outplayed in every aspect of the game and never looked like opening their tally. They were without a few leading players including England internationals Marcus Smith and Alex Dombrandt, but it will take time for them to recover from this.

Ben Loader, Jac Morgan, Will Trenholm, Charlie Atkinson, Seb Atkinson, Will Joseph, Caolon Engefield and George Barton were all on the tryscoring sheet, with Barton converting four.

Leicester clinched their first Gallagher Prem win of the season with a 24-19 victory over Newcastle.

Making his Newcastle bow in front of a sold-out Kingston Park, Obi Ene crossed early on, but the Tigers soon took control as tries from Samiuela Moli and Adam Radwan along with a Billy Searle penalty handed them a 17-5 lead at the break.

George McGuigan went over in the second half for Newcastle, but Will Hurd's try extended Leicester's advantage and they withstood a late scare when Cam Jordan crossed for the hosts in the last 10 minutes.

The Tigers managed to see the game out to move into fifth after two Prem matches, while Newcastle slipped to a second successive league defeat.

articles.title: United Rugby Championship: The Welsh talking points as Cardiff and Dragons start strongly
articles.summary: Which players are impressing as Cardiff and Dragons enjoy strong starts in the United Rugby Championship while Scarlets and Ospreys are still hunting a win.
articles.body:
Only two rounds of the United Rugby Championship (URC) have been completed but it is Cardiff and Dragons who are the early Welsh pacesetters, while Scarlets and Ospreys are languishing at the bottom of the table in 14th and 15th respectively.

Cardiff have won both games and lie second, while Dragons in sixth are unbeaten after winning an entertaining 10-try derby against Scarlets in Newport.

Ospreys and Scarlets are battling for long-term survival, with only one west Wales side set to exist in two years, but currently they would love just a victory after two defeats each.

While Louis Rees-Zammit , Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan continue to star in England's Prem, BBC Sport Wales looks at what has happened in the URC over the weekend.

Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

A year ago Dragons were lamenting missed opportunities in the first block of the season.

Now, aided by the belief built in the second half of 2025-26, they have started to take them.

Filo Tiatia's men are digging deep in tough moments when previously they have folded, with the head coach deserving great credit for that.

"You are not just fighting for the players on the field. There is a deeper understanding in the group around what they are actually fighting for," said Tiatia.

Dragons scored six tries against Scarlets and the driving line-out that earned a late leveller at Benetton was once again a weapon.

There is also variety to their game with balance in wide positions courtesy of the power of new recruit Anzelo Tuitavuki and the pace of Rio Dyer.

Dragons also blew several chances to add to their try tally and can certainly be more clinical in the 22.

"There is lots to grow, lots to improve, but to come away with the points at home was important," said Tiatia.

Dragons will hope to extend their unbeaten start to the campaign with Ospreys and Perpignan visiting Rodney Parade in the URC and Challenge Cup.

With those games followed by a trip to Swansea and a home fixture against Zebre, the first block could give Tiatia's side a launchpad.

Dragons trio continuing Gwent's Tongan tradition

Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies was left to reflect on some familiar problems as his side suffered a second successive defeat.

The continued inability to defend driving line-outs and giving away stupid penalties, typified by the second-half yellow card picked up by captain Josh Macleod, contributed to another loss.

"There were probably three or four big moments which the game turned on," said Davies.

"Those moments added up eventually to a yellow card and we were under pressure in the last 20 minutes."

Scarlets, who also suffered a slow start in 2025-26, are missing influential injured back-row forwards Fletcher Anderson and Taine Plumtree.

"There is no doubt those two are high-quality players and would bring ability and quality to any team," said Davies.

“It would be nice to get them back and have them as options.”

Scarlets face a reunion on Saturday with former head coach Wayne Pivac, who is now coaching a Benetton side also looking for a first victory.

"It is very important," said Davies. "All points are crucial and that's why we're into a massive game next week."

A tour to South Africa to start the season was always going to test Ospreys and they failed to upset the odds against Sharks or Lions.

A four-try bonus in Durban at least got the points tally moving and Mark Jones should profit from team bonding and having given 27 members of his squad starts.

Another big plus came from former Australia captain Liam Wright wearing six on his back in successive professional fixtures for the first time since 2024 after several years of injury misfortune.

The blind-side flanker has already made an impression with his work rate, line-out skills and ability to do the simple stuff well, with his leadership an added bonus.

It could be argued that Ospreys lack big ball carriers – and they will hope to get that from a different department in the coming weeks with the availability of former Australia wing Marika Koroibete – but Wright will be an excellent addition if he stays fit.

There should be plenty more to come as the 28-year-old builds momentum.

Cardiff have claimed nine points from wins against Scarlets and Zebre but their programme will ramp up in the next two weeks.

After defeating teams that finished 14th and 16th in the URC last season, Corniel van Zyl's side will face defending league champions Leinster on Saturday in Dublin before a Champions Cup opener at English Prem winners Northampton.

Cardiff coasted into a 40-8 lead against Zebre but know they cannot afford to repeat the concentration lapse that allowed the Italians to score three tries and 19 points.

"It's something to work on," said Van Zyl. "It's stuff we can control but we take the win. We don't normally have that kind of lead, so it's unfamiliar territory."

Leinster have been in South Africa for the opening two games with narrow defeats by Lions and Sharks, claiming three bonus points.

The Irish province return for the first competitive game at their expensively-redeveloped home, which is now called the Laya Arena and has a capacity of 20,600.

"We know they're a mega club, have very, very good players, good systems and good coaches, so it will be a nice challenge for us," said Van Zyl.

"Hopefully we'll have a few players back. We have eight days this time around, so more time to prepare and recover."

The Zebre fixture was one to remember for 18-year-old Cardiff hooker Tom Howe, who celebrated his Cardiff debut as a replacement.

"It is unbelievable," said Howe. "I have grown up watching these games and my dad used to take me, so to get the chance to come here and play with my family watching is amazing."

WRU seek to sell SRC side RGC to private investors

Wales head coach Steve Tandy will have been an interested observer because he names his Nations Championship squad in 16 days' time.

There are only two more matches for some fringe players to impress, so the past weekend will have been important.

The player-of-the-match, two-try display from Dragons hooker Elliot Dee was timely as he looks to challenge Lake, Ryan Elias, Evan Lloyd and Liam Belcher in the international pecking order.

Scarlets wing Macs Page, who was an unused player in a Wales squad in 2025, demonstrated some of that past form with two tries of his own, including a superb solo effort.

He enjoyed a fascinating battle against Dragons favourite Rio Dyer, who had a mixed first half followed by an outstanding second period where his early kick-off regather set the tone.

Dyer’s searing break later led directly to Macleod‘s yellow card, which helped tip the match in Dragons' favour.

articles.title: Sam Burgess: Warrington head coach says he will stay despite Grand Final loss
articles.summary: Sam Burgess says he plans to stay at Warrington for 2027 as the Wolves try to bounce back from more Grand Final heartache.
articles.body:
Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess confirmed he is going to stay with the club for next year as the dust settles on yet another near miss in the Grand Final.

Saturday's 23-10 loss to Wakefield Trinity means Warrington have been losing finalists five times on Super League's biggest stage.

But having led the Wolves back to Old Trafford for the first time since 2018, Burgess - whose side also suffered narrow Challenge Cup final defeats in 2024 and 2025 - wants the pain to drive them on.

The 37-year-old is yet to agree terms for 2027 and beyond, but he has offered reassurances to the club's owner Simon Moran about his future.

"I've not signed a contract yet but I've given my word to Simon Moran and that's probably better than any contract," said Burgess.

"I truly believe in where we're going as a club and the identity we've created. In the middle of the season, we had 15 players injured and the academy system held us together.

"It'll be the same again next year and I truly believe in our philosophy."

Wakefield beat Warrington to win Super League

'An unbelievable story' - inside unfancied Wakefield's rapid ascent

Quiz: Name every Super League Grand Finalist

That philosophy was characterised by the appearances of scrum-half Ewan Irwin and centre Arron Lindop at Old Trafford.

Irwin is still only 18 and Lindop just two years older - but they contributed all 10 of their side's points against Wakefield with Lindop crossing for both tries and Irwin adding a conversion.

It is the emergence of that duo and others who are waiting in the wings that gives Burgess belief there will not be another eight-year wait to return to the domestic game's biggest stage.

"This is more of a beginning," said the man who won the National Rugby League Premiership in Australia with South Sydney Rabbitohs in 2014.

"We've understood what it takes to get here now - well certainly I have - and the squad we are building now is getting more towards 'my' squad.

"We've understood as a club and a staff what it takes to get here and we're determined to take that next step, but we have got to keep improving.

"I guess we have to let the pain of today drive us forward tomorrow."

For now, that leaves Warrington as the nearly men of rugby league with Wakefield, and not the Wire, becoming the sixth club to join the elite band of Super League winners.

articles.title: NRL Grand Final: Sydney Roosters win 19-18 against Newcastle Knights
articles.summary: Mark Nawaqanitawase scores two tries in his last match before switching back to rugby union to help Sydney Roosters beat Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the NRL Grand Final.
articles.body:
Australian National Rugby League Grand Final

Tries: Nawaqanitawase 2, Smith Goals: Walker 3 Drop goal: Cherry-Evans

Tries: Manuleleua, Ponga, Marzhew Goals: Smith 3

Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries to help Sydney Roosters end the Newcastle Knights' fairytale in the National Rugby League Premiership Grand Final.

Nawaqanitawase, who is stepping away from rugby league and could represent Australia at the rugby union World Cup next year, crossed once in each half to help prevent a big upset in front of a crowd of 80,814 at Stadium Australia.

Newcastle were looking to win a first title since 2001 and become the first club since 1934 to win the Premiership after finishing bottom in the previous season.

A late try from the Knights' Greg Marzhew made it a one-point game, but the Roosters held on to clinch a 16th title and first since 2019 in what was Nawaqanitawase's last game before moving to play union in Japan.

He played union for four years with Super Rugby's Waratahs before switching to rugby league in 2024 to line up for the Roosters, and Sunday's victory was the ideal sign-off as his two-year contract comes to an end.

"Credit to the Knights, they fought for 80 minutes there," said 26-year-old Nawaqanitawase.

"This is going to last me a lifetime. It's sad to go, but I love everyone here, I love all the boys, and let's celebrate this win, far out."

England beware - the Australia try magician who swapped union for league

Nawaqanitawase played 11 times for the Wallabies between 2022 and 2023 before becoming the first union-to-league switcher to feature for the Kangaroos since Scott Gourley in 1991 when he played in last year's Ashes series.

The Knights, who finished three places below the Roosters in the regular season, looked determined not to give Nawaqanitawase his perfect swansong, with Francis Manuleleua and skipper Kalyn Ponga scoring early tries to give them a 12-0 lead.

But Nawaqanitawase cut the deficit with a clever kick and chase five minutes before the break.

Roosters centre Billy Smith forced his way over in the 47th minute for a converted try that levelled the scores at 12-12.

Sam Walker put the Sydney side in front for the first time with a penalty seven minutes later, and Nawaqanitawase added his second try in the right corner before the hour to extend the lead to 18-12.

Daly Cherry-Evans, 37, playing his last NRL game before his switch to Super League side Hull FC for the 2027 season, slotted a drop-goal to extend the advantage to seven points.

Knights summoned the spirit of their sensational semi-final win over Penrith Panthers with 12 men, as Marzhew crossed with four minutes remaining, but they were unable to complete what would have been a famous comeback.

articles.title: The Prem: Saracens 17-21 Sale: Sharks beat Sarries despite red card
articles.summary: Sale overcome Jacques Vermeulen's red card to defeat Saracens 21-17 and pick up their first win of The Prem campaign.
articles.body:
Tries: Mawi, Va'enuku, C Bracken Cons: Burke

Tries: Jibulu, O'Flaherty, Bamber Cons: Ford 2, Lozowski

Sale overcame Jacques Vermeulen's red card to defeat Saracens and pick up their first win of The Prem campaign.

Sarries struggled to break down a stubborn Sharks defence despite having numerical superiority for 27 minutes of the first half after Alex Lozowski's yellow and Vermeulen's 20-minute red card.

Incredibly, Sale took a 7-5 lead into half-time thanks to Nathan Jibulu's early converted try, despite Eroni Mawi's reply, and then went further ahead soon after the break as Tom O'Flaherty raced in.

Ben Bamber stretched Sale's lead to 11 points after Sione Va'enuku had cut the gap, and though Charlie Bracken's late score again put the game in the balance, the hosts held on.

After shipping 150 points to Saracens in two Prem hammerings last season, Sale's victory at the Stone X was built on a huge defensive effort.

Their forwards laid down an impressive early marker when a driving maul carved through Sarries with relative ease to sweep Jibulu over the line.

But the visitors were soon down to 13 as former Sarrie Alex Lozowski was yellow-carded for a high shot on Barbeary on his first Sale start before Vermeulen was red-carded for putting a shoulder into Tomos Williams' head.

And only a TMO intervention prevented the visitors going down to 12 when Hamish Smales overturned Courtney Lawes' yellow card for a deliberate knock on.

Smales was involved again to overturn Nick Tompkins' smart close-range finish for a Nick Isiekwe's obstruction in the build-up, but Mawi finally turned Sarries' red-zone pressure into points when he powered over.

Yet Sale were heartened to head into half-time with a two-point lead and back up to full strength as Elia Canakaivata replaced Vermeulen.

Saracens responded with three changes at half-time, including a debut for England lock George Martin, but Sale soon went nine points clear when O'Flaherty collected George Ford's up and under on halfway and raced away to score.

The hosts finally found their cutting edge when a quick switch of play while camped on the Sale line created an overlap and gave Va'Enuku a walk-in on debut.

Sale's defence continued to impress before a quick change of pace in attack sent them 21-10 up as Ford teed up Bamber to run a hard line through a gap and race in.

Once again the Sarries response was swift as Jack Bracken cut in off the right wing to give brother Charlie a clear run to the line to set up a tense finale.

Venter explains wine reference as job title confirmed

Despite opening the season with an eventful and impressive 40-38 win over Leicester , Brendan Venter made most of the headlines in its aftermath.

The former South Africa international was reported to have changed his job title to head of rugby culture and wine consultant after failing to follow media commitments at the league's season launch and opening match.

Sarries new chief executive Ed Coetzee on Friday ended the confusion on Friday by confirming Venter as head of culture and technical director, a role which will include "significant media duties".

Venter duly spoke to TNT Sports before the clash with Sale and said he refused the director's title because he had "absolutely nothing" to do with other sections of the club such as the academy and women's section.

The 56-year-old also insisted the wine consultant reference was not a joke aimed at the media.

"Our whole theme this year was all about wine," Venter told TNT Sports. "Everything in our theme was about a blend and getting the blend right.

"There's nobody in life that is successful by doing one thing the whole time, it doesn't work like that. As you grow older you have to blend things so that's where it came from, and it's very relevant."

Chris Jones, BBC Rugby Union correspondent

The Prem has been all about free flowing attack so far this season, but this was much more of an old school dogfight.

A stop-start game dominated by the referee's whistle, Sale came up with two big plays in the second half: Tom O'Flaherty with a stunning individual score, while Ben Bamber's try was also a beauty after excellent build-up play.

The big names stepped up for Sale. Courtney Lawes looked his old self in the lineout and on the floor, while Tom Curry was magnificent in the kind of physical scrap he relishes. George Ford managed the game beautifully in the closing stages.

Sarries director of rugby turned wine consultant turned technical director Brendan Venter again handed media duties over to head coach Joe Shaw post-match, but he will talk this week in a bid to avoid further sanctions from Prem Rugby.

'Jibulu could explode onto international scene' - reaction

"We couldn't really get into our flow, that's the truth of it. Credit to Sale, they came and fronted up.

"They had adversity, which we had last weekend, but they kept coming. We have to take it on the chin and move on."

"Any time you watch Nathan (Jibulu) play he makes an impact.

"He was a wrecking ball and caused havoc around the field. He nailed his line-outs and showed he's of international class.

"You can get away with being fast and skilful in the Prem, but it's another level again in terms of the power that's required at international level and he's got that ability. He's immensely strong.

"This could be the season when he explodes onto the international scene."

Saracens: Daly; J Bracken, Tompkins, Va'enuku, Segun; Burke, Williams; Mawi, Dan, Street, Itoje (c), Tizard, Isiekwe, Gonzalez, Barbeary.

Replacements: Clarke, O'Driscoll, Clarey, Martin, Michelow, Earl, C Bracken, Malins.

Sale: Carpenter; O'Flaherty, Marchant, Lozowski, Reed; Ford, Warr; Smith, Jibulu, Opoku-Fordjour, Van Rhyn (c), Bamber, Lawes, Curry, Vermeulen.

Replacements: Caine, McIntyre, Francis, Tshiunza, Canakaivata, Hanson, Louw, Loganimasi.

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Sale Sharks defy Jacques Vermeulen's first-half red card to beat Saracens
articles.summary: Sale Sharks' Jacques Vermeulen received a 20-minute red card for a tackle on Tomos Williams in the first half; Sale's Alex Lozowski had also seen yellow for a similar offence; Sale managed to hold on and get the win
articles.body:
Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.

Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O'Flaherty produced the match's pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try.

It was part of a dominant second half from Sale, who capitalised on the hosts' lifeless performance to bounce back after losing to Bristol on the opening weekend with their hooker Nathan Jibulu also outstanding.

Referee Joe James and TMO Hamish Smales experienced a busy opening half an hour, issuing two cards and disallowing a Saracens try.

It had started so well for Sale when Jibulu finished a driving maul but soon after centre Lozowski was sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on Alfie Barbeary, who was forced off for an HIA.

Worse was to come when Vermeulen was given his marching orders for a dangerous challenge on Williams as the Sharks looked to press home an attack down the right touchline.

It meant Saracens were given the opportunity to play against 13 for three minutes and Sale's situation would have deteriorated further had Courtney Lawes not seen an attempted deliberate knock go backwards.

Almost immediately the hosts appeared to have taken advantage but a Nick Tompkins try was ruled out because of obstruction by Nick Isiekwe and it was not until Eroni Mawi bundled over in the 34th minute that they were off the mark.

For all Saracens' sustained pressure they still trailed 7-5 and a minute into the second half that became 14-5 after O'Flaherty caught a George Ford up and under that went sideways and then slipped through the home defence before sprinting over.

Sale ran out of tacklers to enable Sione Va'enuku to strike back almost immediately but they resumed on the front foot and were frustrated to be penalised just short of the whitewash on two occasions.

They continued knocking on the door and suddenly changed pace with a series of runs gaining yards until Ford sent Ben Bamber galloping over.

Sale now led 21-10 and Saracens' dismal afternoon continued when Theo Dan limped off while his fellow hooker Jamie George watched from the stands, sidelined by injury.

Charlie Bracken combined with brother Jack to race over with eight minutes to go and the Sharks then let another commanding position slip away because of a penalty close to the line, but they had already done enough to see off Saracens.

articles.title: Rugby fans descend on Wakefield for celebratory bus parade
articles.summary: The city has been alive with celebrations after Trinity brought home the Super League trophy.
articles.body:
Thousands of rugby league fans turned out to watch an open-top bus parade, after Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions.

Trinity beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in Saturday's Grand Final at Old Trafford - their first title win since 1968, long before Super League was established.

To celebrate the victory, two buses, carrying players and staff, travelled from the club's ground at Belle Vue to Wakefield Town Hall for a civic reception.

Fullback Max Jowitt, who has made 188 appearances for Trinity and scored three goals in the final, said the parade had been an "unbelievable" experience.

"The fans have been unbelievable, the city is unbelievable and the trophy's unbelievable," he said.

Fans lined city centre streets to see the buses, which arrived at Wakefield Town Hall at about 15:00.

Jane Robinson became a Wakefield Trinity fan through her late husband, who supported the side from childhood.

She was at the game at Old Trafford, where the team became only the sixth club to win the Super League title.

"It was absolutely out of this world - the atmosphere was electric," she said.

"You can't help but think how good this has been for Wakefield."

Also revelling in the excitement from being at the game, young fan Jasper was wearing a tri-coloured wig his grandfather bought him.

He said "everyone was screaming and shouting" each time Trinity scored a try.

"It's amazing - it's an incredible feeling," added his mum Sarah.

Claire Slater, who was watching alongside her son Cohen, said she felt "absolutely ecstatic".

"The atmosphere yesterday at the ground was absolutely electric, so we wanted to come for the atmosphere today. It's been years in the making hasn't it?"

Melvyn Moyes, who was in the city centre with his brother Ken to cheer on the team, described the atmosphere as "buzzing".

"I can remember the good old days – and the bad old days," Melvyn said.

"Wakefield is back – look out everybody."

Following the reception, a free ticketed fan celebration was held at WX on Union Street with player appearances, speeches and highlights from the Grand Final on big screens.
